title: On the Quantisation of Linear Gauge Theories on Lorentzian Manifolds: Maxwell's Theory via Complete Gauge Fixing
comment: PhD Thesis, University of Genoa, Italy. xviii + 252 pages, 4 figures. The results are based in part on [arXiv:2401.08403] and [arXiv:2507.05004]; to a lesser extend, the thesis draws on aspects from [arXiv:2407.07576] and [arXiv:2507.11965]. This is an updated version of the PhD thesis defended in February 2026 and incorporates minor corrections over the original at hdl.handle.net/11567/1286476
summary:
This thesis is devoted to the study of hyperbolic differential operators on globally hyperbolic manifolds, linear gauge theories and their quantisation.
  In the first part, we treat the Cauchy problem for symmetric hyperbolic systems and normally hyperbolic operators on globally hyperbolic manifolds from first principles. Although hyperbolic equations are usually studied with local interactions, there are strong motivations from several areas of mathematical physics to consider also nonlocal interactions. As an intermezzo, we therefore take a small deviation from the classical local theory and prove well-posedness of the Cauchy problem for symmetric hyperbolic systems coupled to a broad class of nonlocal potentials.
  The second part presents a detailed exposition of linear gauge theories in globally hyperbolic spacetimes. Linear gauge theories are yet another deviation from the concept of hyperbolicity: the corresponding equations of motion are generically non-hyperbolic; however, can always be reduced to a constrained hyperbolic dynamics once an appropriate gauge fixing procedure has been applied. We give a thorough analysis of their Cauchy problem and classical phase space, complemented by a detailed discussion of many examples of physical interest, and discuss their quantisation following the algebraic approach to quantum field theory.
  The final chapter is devoted to the quantisation of Maxwell's theory on globally hyperbolic spacetimes, with the goal of proving the existence of Hadamard states. The novelty of our approach lies in a new gauge-fixing procedure at the level of initial data, which allows us to suppress the unphysical degrees of freedom. This gauge is achieved by means of a new Hodge decomposition for differential k-forms in Sobolev spaces on complete Riemannian manifolds, while states are constructed using tools from pseudodifferential calculus.

AI.tldr: This thesis studies hyperbolic differential operators, linear gauge theories, and their quantisation on globally hyperbolic manifolds; it extends well-posedness results to nonlocal symmetric hyperbolic systems, provides a comprehensive analysis of classical and quantum linear gauge theories—including Maxwell’s theory—and introduces a novel gauge-fixing method based on a Sobolev Hodge decomposition to construct Hadamard states.
AI.motivation: To rigorously treat hyperbolic PDEs and gauge theories in curved spacetimes with mathematical precision; to address physical needs for nonlocal interactions and well-defined quantisation (especially Hadamard states) in algebraic QFT.
AI.method: Analytical PDE theory (Cauchy problem, symmetric hyperbolic systems, normally hyperbolic operators), gauge-fixing via constraint analysis and novel Hodge decomposition in Sobolev spaces, algebraic QFT framework, pseudodifferential calculus for state construction.
AI.result: Well-posedness of Cauchy problem for nonlocal symmetric hyperbolic systems; complete characterization of classical phase space for linear gauge theories; rigorous quantisation scheme; existence proof of Hadamard states for Maxwell theory via new initial-data gauge fixing and Sobolev Hodge decomposition.
AI.conclusion: The thesis unifies geometric PDE theory, classical gauge dynamics, and algebraic quantisation on globally hyperbolic spacetimes, introducing key technical innovations—especially the Sobolev Hodge decomposition and nonlocal well-posedness—that enable robust, physically meaningful QFT constructions.

title: The quantum group structure of long-range integrable deformations
summary: Quantum integrable spin chains are known to possess a large family of long-range deformations generated by the local, boost and bilocal operators. Although these deformations are well-understood on the level of the pairwise commuting charges, the underlying quantum group structures had not yet been recognised. In this paper, we provide a quantum group-theoretical description for the family of long-range deformations of arbitrary homogeneous Yang-Baxter integrable spin chains up to first order in the deformation parameter. In particular, we show that the deformations are obtained via a twist of the algebraic structure of the underlying quantum group. This twisting results in a generally non-associative algebra that has a non-trivial Drinfeld associator. The Drinfeld associator is then shown to encode the information about the long-range interaction terms for the integrable spin chain. Moreover, the deformed quantum group is shown to contain a large perturbatively associative substructure, thus ensuring the perturbative integrability of the long-range model. The deformed quantum group provides explicit expressions for the Lax operators and R-matrices of the long-range deformed models, which manifestly satisfy the RLL relation and the Yang-Baxter equation up to first order in the deformation parameter. In order to derive the results, we introduce algebra elements that we call the algebraic charge densities. As a side result, we provide a conjecture for the explicit expressions of the undeformed charge densities in terms of these algebra elements.

AI.tldr: This paper provides a quantum group-theoretical description of first-order long-range deformations of homogeneous Yang–Baxter integrable spin chains, showing they arise from a twist yielding a generally non-associative algebra with a Drinfeld associator encoding long-range interactions; the deformed structure retains a perturbatively associative subalgebra ensuring integrability and yields explicit Lax operators and R-matrices satisfying RLL and Yang–Baxter equations to first order.
AI.motivation: To uncover the underlying quantum group structures governing long-range deformations of integrable spin chains—previously understood only at the level of commuting charges but lacking a systematic algebraic (quantum group) characterization.
AI.method: Constructs a twisted quantum group structure using algebraic charge densities; analyzes the resulting non-associative algebra and its Drinfeld associator; verifies perturbative associativity of a substructure; derives deformed Lax operators and R-matrices satisfying the RLL relation and Yang–Baxter equation to first order in the deformation parameter.
AI.result: Long-range deformations are realized as twists of the underlying quantum group, producing a non-associative algebra governed by a Drinfeld associator that encodes interaction range; a perturbatively associative subalgebra ensures integrability; explicit first-order deformed Lax operators and R-matrices are obtained, satisfying required algebraic relations; algebraic charge densities are introduced, enabling a conjecture for undeformed charge densities.
AI.conclusion: The family of long-range deformations admits a coherent quantum group description via twisting, unifying structural insights (non-associativity, Drinfeld associator) with physical requirements (perturbative integrability, consistency of RLL/Yang–Baxter), and establishes algebraic charge densities as fundamental building blocks for constructing both deformed and undeformed conserved charges.

title: Dynamical delocalization in disordered 2D Chern insulators
summary: We show the existence of energies exhibiting dynamical delocalization in discrete 2D Chern insulators perturbed by a random potential in a general setting. Our proof exploits two main features of the model: jumps in the integer value of the Chern character and continuity of averaged spectral projections in both energy and disorder parameters. This allows us to show robustness of the topological index in the presence of disorder, which, combined with existing methods to prove dynamical localization, allows us to provide detailed information on the phase diagram of the model. The novelty of our approach is that we are able to show dynamical delocalization in the disorder parameter, and not only in the energy parameter, which allows to prove Anderson metal-insulator transition even when spectral gaps close due to the strength of disorder.

AI.tldr: This paper proves dynamical delocalization in disordered 2D Chern insulators by leveraging topological robustness (Chern number jumps and continuity of averaged spectral projections), enabling demonstration of an Anderson metal-insulator transition even when spectral gaps close.
AI.motivation: To establish rigorous evidence of dynamical delocalization—and thus an Anderson metal-insulator transition—in 2D discrete Chern insulators under generic random disorder, especially in regimes where spectral gaps vanish due to strong disorder, where conventional localization-based arguments fail.
AI.method: Functional analytic approach combining topological K-theory (Chern character jumps), continuity properties of disorder-averaged spectral projections in energy and disorder strength, and comparison with known dynamical localization criteria; constructs a phase diagram via topological index stability under perturbation.
AI.result: Proof of dynamical delocalization occurring robustly across a nontrivial interval of the disorder parameter (not just energy), implying existence of extended states and an Anderson transition even when spectral gaps are closed by disorder.
AI.conclusion: Topological invariants (Chern character) remain well-defined and stable under disorder, serving as a diagnostic for delocalized dynamics; this yields a general mechanism for disorder-driven metal-insulator transitions in topological insulators beyond the clean or weak-disorder regimes.

title: Hamilton--Jacobi theory for non-conservative field theories in the $k$-contact framework
summary: This article develops a Hamilton--Jacobi theory for non-conservative classical field theories, with particular emphasis on dissipative systems, in the framework of co-oriented k-contact geometry. We introduce evolution k-contact k-vector fields, extending the contact evolution formalism to field theories, and analyse the corresponding Hamilton--De Donder--Weyl equations. Moreover, we develop two distinct families of Hamilton--Jacobi theories: a z-independent approach, based on the reconstruction of the dynamics from an integrable k-vector field defined on the base manifold of $(\bigoplus^kT^*Q)\times\mathbb{R}^k\to Q$, and a z-dependent approach, where the integrable k-vector field is defined on the base manifold of $(\bigoplus^kT^*Q)\times\mathbb{R}^k\to Q\times\mathbb{R}^k$. We develop in detail the important case of Hamiltonian functions with affine dependence on the dissipative variables, show how quadratic dependence on these variables can be used structurally to enlarge the range of applications, and recover the ordinary contact Hamilton--Jacobi theory as the particular case k=1, while removing some technical assumptions appearing in previous formulations. Our theory is illustrated through several representative examples, including the telegrapher/Klein--Gordon equation, a dissipative Hunter--Saxton equation, a simple dissipative non-regular first-order field model, and a relativistic thermodynamic model.

AI.tldr: This paper extends Hamilton–Jacobi theory to non-conservative classical field theories—especially dissipative ones—using co-oriented k-contact geometry; it introduces evolution k-contact k-vector fields, derives generalized Hamilton–De Donder–Weyl equations, and constructs two Hamilton–Jacobi formulations (z-independent and z-dependent), illustrating them on physical models like dissipative Klein–Gordon and Hunter–Saxton equations.
AI.motivation: To formulate a geometric Hamilton–Jacobi theory for non-conservative (dissipative) classical field theories, overcoming limitations of existing contact-based approaches and generalizing from mechanics (k=1) to higher-dimensional field theories while accommodating affine and quadratic dissipative structures.
AI.method: Uses co-oriented k-contact geometry to define evolution k-contact k-vector fields; derives Hamilton–De Donder–Weyl equations; constructs two Hamilton–Jacobi frameworks—one with base manifold Q and one with Q×ℝᵏ—depending on whether the generating function depends on dissipative coordinates z; analyzes affine and quadratic Hamiltonian dependence on z; verifies consistency by recovering standard contact HJ theory at k=1.
AI.result: A fully geometric, coordinate-free Hamilton–Jacobi theory for dissipative field theories; explicit characterization of integrable k-vector fields in both z-independent and z-dependent settings; extension to affine and structurally useful quadratic dissipative couplings; recovery of standard contact HJ theory as k=1 without prior technical assumptions; validation via physically relevant examples including telegrapher/Klein–Gordon, dissipative Hunter–Saxton, non-regular field model, and relativistic thermodynamics.
AI.conclusion: The proposed k-contact Hamilton–Jacobi framework provides a rigorous, flexible, and unifying geometric foundation for dissipative classical field theories, significantly generalizing previous contact mechanical results and enabling systematic treatment of irreversible field dynamics.

title: Topological Susceptibility and QCD at Finite Theta Angle
comment: 26 pages, 4 figures, invited chapter for the Encyclopedia of Nuclear Physics
summary: In this chapter we provide a pedagogical introduction to the main theoretical aspects related to topology and $θ$-dependence in Quantum Chromo-Dynamics (QCD), and to their phenomenological relevance in the Standard Model ($η^\prime$ physics, neutron electric dipole moment) and beyond (strong CP problem and the axion solution). We then provide an overview of the main analytic predictions for $θ$-dependence obtained using several different approaches (chiral effective theories, large-$N$ arguments, semiclassical methods) and their regimes of validity, as well as a selection of the most recent numerical results about QCD topology obtained via Monte Carlo simulations of the lattice-discretized theory.

AI.tldr: This chapter offers a pedagogical review of topology and θ-dependence in QCD, covering theoretical foundations, phenomenological implications (e.g., η′ mass, neutron EDM, strong CP problem, axions), analytic predictions from chiral effective theories, large-N, and semiclassical methods, and recent lattice QCD Monte Carlo results on topological observables.
AI.motivation: To provide a unified, accessible exposition of QCD topology and θ-dependence—central to the strong CP problem—and bridge theoretical frameworks with phenomenology and modern lattice simulations.
AI.method: Pedagogical review combining analytical approaches (chiral perturbation theory, large-N expansion, instanton calculus) with numerical lattice QCD Monte Carlo methods; comparative analysis of validity regimes.
AI.result: Synthesis of analytic θ-dependence predictions across different approximations and summary of state-of-the-art lattice results on topological charge distribution, susceptibility, and autocorrelation.
AI.conclusion: Topology and θ-dependence are essential for understanding nonperturbative QCD; analytic and lattice methods complement each other, but challenges remain in controlling topological freezing and continuum extrapolation in simulations.

title: Observation of a Doubly-strange Hyperon $Ξ(1720)$ in $J/ψ\rightarrow{}K^{-}Σ^0\barΞ^{+}+c.c.$
summary: Based on a sample of $(10087 \pm 44) \times 10^6$ $J/ψ$ events collected with the BESIII detector at BEPCII, we report the first observation of the decay $J/ψ\rightarrow K^- Σ^0 \barΞ^++c.c.$. A partial wave analysis is performed to investigate the involved excited states. In addition to the well-established $Ξ(1690)$, a new doubly-strange hyperon $Ξ(1720) $ is observed decaying to $K^- Σ^0$ with a mass of $1721.0 \pm 5.2_{\rm stat.} \pm 3.4_{\rm syst.} ~{\rm MeV}/c^2$ and a width of $31.3 \pm 18.3_{\rm stat.} \pm 15.4_{\rm syst.} ~{\rm MeV}$, with a statistical significance exceeding $10σ$. The spin-parity hypothesis testing across various quantum number configurations reveals that the spin-parity of $Ξ(1720)$ favors $J^P = {\frac{3}{2}}^+$. Furthermore, the branching fraction of $J/ψ\rightarrow K^- Σ^0 \barΞ^++c.c.$ is determined to be $(2.68 \pm 0.04_{\rm stat.} \pm 0.17_{\rm syst.}) \times 10^{-5}$.

AI.tldr: First observation of J/ψ → K⁻Σ⁰Ξ̄⁺⁺ + c.c. decay; discovery of a new doubly-strange hyperon Ξ(1720) with mass 1721.0 ± 5.2 ± 3.4 MeV/c², width 31.3 ± 18.3 ± 15.4 MeV, and favored J^P = 3/2⁺; branching fraction measured as (2.68 ± 0.04 ± 0.17) × 10⁻⁵.
AI.motivation: To explore the spectrum of doubly-strange hyperons and test QCD-inspired models via charmonium decays, where J/ψ provides a clean gluon-rich environment for hadron spectroscopy.
AI.method: Analysis of (10087 ± 44) × 10⁶ J/ψ events from BESIII; full reconstruction of K⁻Σ⁰Ξ̄⁺⁺ + c.c.; amplitude-based partial wave analysis (PWA) to isolate resonant structures in the K⁻Σ⁰ system; spin-parity hypothesis testing using likelihood ratio tests across J^P assignments.
AI.result: Discovery of Ξ(1720) with >10σ significance; mass = 1721.0 ± 5.2(stat.) ± 3.4(syst.) MeV/c², width = 31.3 ± 18.3(stat.) ± 15.4(syst.) MeV; J^P = 3/2⁺ strongly favored; observation of Ξ(1690) confirmed; branching fraction ℬ(J/ψ → K⁻Σ⁰Ξ̄⁺⁺ + c.c.) = (2.68 ± 0.04 ± 0.17) × 10⁻⁵.
AI.conclusion: The Ξ(1720) is a new excited state in the Ξ baryon spectrum, likely a candidate for the first radial or orbital excitation; its properties challenge existing quark model predictions and provide critical input for lattice QCD and coupled-channel calculations.

title: $\mathcal{H}$olographic $\mathcal{N}$aturalness and Information See-Saw Mechanism for Neutrinos
summary: The microscopic origin of the de Sitter entropy remains a central puzzle in quantum gravity related to the cosmological constant problem. Within $\mathcal{H}$olographic $\mathcal{N}$aturalness, we propose this entropy is carried by light, coherent degrees of freedom - "hairons" - emerging as moduli of gravitational instantons on orbifolds. From the Euclidean de Sitter instanton ($S^4$), we construct a new class of orbifold gravitational instantons, $S^4/\mathbb{Z}_N$, where $N$ corresponds to the de Sitter entropy. The moduli space dimension scales linearly with $N$, and we identify these moduli with hairon fields. A $\mathbb{Z}_N$ symmetry from Wilson loops ensures mode distinguishability, yielding the correct entropy. Hairons acquire a mass of the order of the Hubble scale with negligible interactions, suggesting the de Sitter vacuum is a Bose-Einstein condensate of these excitations. We then unify the neutrino mass generation with the cosmological constant via gravitational topology. The small neutrino mass emerges naturally without new physics beyond the Standard Model. The gravitational Chern-Simons structure and anomaly force a topological Higgs mechanism, leading to neutrino condensation via $S^4/\mathbb{Z}_N$ instantons. The topological degrees $N \sim M_\text{P}^2/Λ\sim 10^{120}$ provide both a holographic entropy counting and a $1/N$ information see-saw mechanism for neutrino masses. Predictions: (i) neutrino superfluid condensation forming Cooper pairs below meV as cold dark matter; (ii) resolution of the strong CP problem via a QCD composite axion; (iii) time-varying neutrino masses tracking th dark energy evolution; (iv) signatures in astroparticle physics, ultra-high-energy cosmic rays and high magnetic field experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes 'hairons'—light, coherent degrees of freedom arising as moduli of orbifold gravitational instantons $S^4/\mathbb{Z}_N$—as the microscopic carriers of de Sitter entropy; it unifies cosmological constant scale, neutrino mass generation, and dark matter via topological gravity, yielding testable predictions including neutrino superfluidity and a composite QCD axion.
AI.motivation: To resolve the microscopic origin of de Sitter entropy and its connection to the cosmological constant problem, while simultaneously explaining the smallness of neutrino masses without beyond-Standard-Model physics.
AI.method: Constructs orbifold Euclidean gravitational instantons $S^4/\mathbb{Z}_N$; identifies their moduli space (dimension ∝ N) with light scalar 'hairon' fields; imposes $\mathbb{Z}_N$ Wilson-loop symmetry for distinguishability; uses gravitational Chern–Simons structure and anomalies to induce a topological Higgs mechanism leading to neutrino condensation; links $N \sim M_\text{P}^2/\Lambda$ to both holographic entropy and a $1/N$ information see-saw for neutrino masses.
AI.result: Derives de Sitter entropy $S_{dS} = N$ from moduli counting; shows hairons form a Bose–Einstein condensate at Hubble-scale mass; explains neutrino masses $m_\nu \sim \Lambda / M_\text{P} \sim 10^{-3}\,\text{eV}$ via topological $1/N$ suppression; predicts neutrino superfluid dark matter, composite axion solving strong CP, time-varying $m_\nu$, and observable astroparticle signatures.
AI.conclusion: De Sitter entropy and neutrino mass are unified through gravitational topology: the same orbifold instanton structure $S^4/\mathbb{Z}_N$ provides both holographic entropy counting and a natural, anomaly-driven seesaw, embedding dark energy, dark matter, and neutrino physics into quantum gravitational geometry.

title: The Hawking Singularity Theorem for Hölder Continuous Metrics with $L^p$-Bounded Curvature
summary:
We prove a low-regularity version of Hawking's singularity theorem for Lorentzian metrics in $W^{1,p}$ with Riemann curvature in $L^p$, where $p>2n$ and $n$ the dimension of spacetime. This extends previous results beyond the Lipschitz regime. Under suitable lower Ricci bounds and upper mean curvature assumptions, expressed in terms of temporal functions, we establish both the globally hyperbolic version of Hawking's theorem, in the form of an upper bound on the time separation from a spacelike Cauchy hypersurface, and the version with a compact achronal spacelike hypersurface, yielding timelike RT-geodesic incompleteness.
  The proof combines regularisations, based on the elliptic RT-equations, to raise the regularity of the metric by one derivative, with a refinement of the previously used manifold convolution. We introduce a new smeared-out notion of mean curvature adapted to the low metric regularity before, and the $W^{2,p}$-hypersurfaces arising after regularisation. As further consequences, we show that $W^{1,p}$-Lorentzian metrics with $L^p$-bounded curvature are causally plain, and we prove a corresponding low-regularity version of Myers's theorem in the Riemannian setting.

AI.tldr: This paper proves a low-regularity version of Hawking's singularity theorem for Lorentzian metrics in $W^{1,p}$ with Riemann curvature in $L^p$ ($p > 2n$), extending beyond Lipschitz regularity; it establishes timelike geodesic incompleteness under lower Ricci bounds and upper mean curvature assumptions, using elliptic RT-equation-based regularisation and a novel smeared mean curvature notion.
AI.motivation: To extend Hawking's classical singularity theorem to spacetime metrics with minimal regularity—specifically below Lipschitz—where standard geometric tools (e.g., connection coefficients, curvature tensors) are not classically defined, yet physically relevant for shock wave spacetimes and generalised solutions of Einstein’s equations.
AI.method: Combines metric regularisation via the elliptic RT-equations (raising regularity from $W^{1,p}$ to $W^{2,p}$), manifold convolution techniques, and introduces a smeared-out definition of mean curvature suitable for $W^{1,p}$ metrics and their $W^{2,p}$ regularisations; employs temporal functions to formulate synthetic Ricci and mean curvature bounds in low regularity.
AI.result: Proves both globally hyperbolic and compact achronal versions of Hawking’s theorem for $W^{1,p}$-Lorentzian metrics ($p > 2n$); shows such metrics are causally plain; derives a low-regularity Myers-type theorem in the Riemannian case.
AI.conclusion: Hawking’s singularity theorem holds robustly under significantly weakened differentiability assumptions, confirming that timelike geodesic incompleteness—and thus singularity formation—is not an artifact of high smoothness but persists even for weakly regular spacetimes satisfying synthetic curvature bounds.

title: Topological and self-dual vortices in a double sigma model with Maxwell coupling
summary: In this work, we construct a double O(3)-sigma model minimally coupled to a Maxwell field in (2+1)-dimensional spacetime and investigate the existence of self-dual magnetic vortex solutions. An analysis of the Bogomol'nyi-Prasad-Sommerfield (BPS) property reveals that both sigma fields belong to the same topological sector and that the potential assumes a periodic cosine-like form. Furthermore, the theory supports the emergence of magnetic vortices with quantized flux, described by two nonlinear O(3)-sigma sectors that effectively combine into a single topological sector in the BPS regime. In addition, we analytically verify the consistency of the BPS structure and its asymptotic behavior. Within this framework, numerical vortex solutions confirm that the field profiles are smooth and spatially localized, with both the magnetic field and the energy density remaining regular and localized.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a double O(3)-sigma model coupled to Maxwell electrodynamics in 2+1D and derives self-dual (BPS) magnetic vortex solutions with quantized flux, where two O(3) sectors merge topologically in the BPS limit; analytical consistency and asymptotics are verified, and numerical solutions confirm smooth, localized field profiles and regular energy/magnetic density.
AI.motivation: To explore self-dual magnetic vortex solutions in a (2+1)D gauge-coupled multi-sigma-model framework, extending beyond single-sector O(3) models and probing novel topological and BPS structures.
AI.method: Construction of a double O(3)-sigma model minimally coupled to Maxwell electrodynamics in (2+1)D; derivation and analysis of Bogomol'nyi-Prasad-Sommerfield (BPS) equations; analytical verification of BPS consistency and asymptotic behavior; numerical computation of vortex solutions.
AI.result: Existence of self-dual magnetic vortices with quantized magnetic flux; both O(3) sigma fields reside in the same topological sector; scalar potential takes a periodic cosine-like form; two nonlinear sigma sectors effectively unify into a single topological sector at the BPS level; numerical solutions show smooth, spatially localized profiles with regular, localized magnetic field and energy density.
AI.conclusion: The double O(3)-sigma–Maxwell system in (2+1)D admits consistent, topologically nontrivial, self-dual magnetic vortex solutions; the BPS structure unifies the two sigma sectors topologically, and the full solution set is analytically tractable and numerically robust.

title: Hypergeometric Functions of Nilpotent Operators: Functional Collapse and Structural Depth at Exceptional Points
comment: 20 pp. Preprint also available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19904809
summary: We study hypergeometric functions of nilpotent operators in finite-dimensional settings, motivated by the algebraic structure of exceptional points in non-Hermitian quantum mechanics. Our starting point is the following exact result: if N is a nilpotent operator of index m+1 in an associative algebra over C, then every generalized hypergeometric function pFq evaluated at N reduces to a finite polynomial in N of degree at most m, without any analytic convergence requirement. This "functional collapse" is distinct from the classical parameter-termination mechanism and arises purely from the nilpotent structure of the argument. The main result is a "nilpotent depth criterion" (Theorem 2): if the first non-constant coefficient of a formal series F appears in degree r >= 1, then the nilpotent part F(N) - F(0)I has nilpotency index bounded above by ceil((m+1)/r). We apply this criterion to Hamiltonians at exceptional points, where H = lambda I + N with N^{m+1} = 0. Theorem 3 establishes that a function F analytic at lambda reduces the Jordan depth of the exceptional point from m+1 to at most ceil((m+1)/r), where r is the contact order of F at lambda. As consequences: the time evolution operator e^{tH} preserves the full Jordan depth for all t != 0; a function with a zero of order m+1 at lambda annihilates the entire Jordan structure; and the order of the pole of the modified resolvent is reduced from m+1 to at most m+1-r. Results are illustrated with explicit 3x3 Jordan block computations for 1F1, 2F1, and the time evolution operator, confirming sharpness of the bounds.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes that generalized hypergeometric functions evaluated on nilpotent operators collapse to finite polynomials due to algebraic nilpotency, not analytic convergence; it introduces a 'nilpotent depth criterion' bounding the nilpotency index of F(N)−F(0)I by ⌈(m+1)/r⌉, where r is the order of the first non-constant term in F's expansion; this yields precise control over Jordan structure reduction in non-Hermitian quantum Hamiltonians at exceptional points.
AI.motivation: To understand the algebraic role of nilpotent operators—arising from Jordan blocks at exceptional points in non-Hermitian quantum mechanics—in generalized hypergeometric functions, beyond classical analytic convergence constraints.
AI.method: Algebraic analysis of formal power series applied to nilpotent operators in finite-dimensional associative algebras over ℂ; derivation of structural bounds using degree-wise coefficient analysis and Jordan canonical form; explicit matrix computations for 3×3 Jordan blocks to verify sharpness.
AI.result: 1) Any pFq(N) reduces exactly to a degree-≤m polynomial when N^{m+1}=0; 2) Nilpotent depth criterion: if F(z) = F(0) + a_r(z−λ)^r + … with a_r ≠ 0, then F(N)−F(0)I has nilpotency index ≤ ⌈(m+1)/r⌉; 3) For H = λI + N, this controls Jordan depth reduction under functional calculus; e.g., e^{tH} preserves full depth, while an m+1-order zero annihilates the Jordan structure; resolvent pole order drops from m+1 to ≤ m+1−r.
AI.conclusion: The functional behavior of analytic functions on nilpotent operators is governed entirely by the interplay between the operator’s nilpotency index and the contact order (vanishing order) of the function at the spectral point—revealing a purely algebraic mechanism for Jordan structure simplification, with direct implications for dynamics and spectral analysis at exceptional points.

title: Deeply virtual pion production through two-loop order
summary: Deeply virtual meson production (DVMP) is among the most prominent channels to extract the nucleon's generalized parton distributions (GPDs) at $ep$ scattering facilities such as {\tt JLab} and the upcoming {\tt EIC/EicC} experiments, which plays a vital role in unravelling the three-dimensional internal structure of nucleon. In this work we calculate for the first time the next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) QCD radiative corrections to the DV$π$P processes $γ_L^* p\to π^+ n$ and $γ_L^* p\to π^0 p$ in the generalized Bjorken limit $Q^2\gg \vert t\vert, Λ_{\text{QCD}}^2$, accurate at the leading twist within collinear factorization framework. The impact of the two-loop QCD corrections appears to be positive and substantial, including which considerably improves the agreement between the perturbative QCD prediction and the available {\tt JLab} data. In addition to the differential longitudinal DV$π$P cross section, we also study the impact of the two-loop QCD corrections on the transverse single-spin asymmetries (TSSA) in some benchmark kinematics at {\tt JLab}, {\tt EIC} and {\tt EicC}.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the first NNLO QCD corrections to deeply virtual pion production (DVπP) processes, significantly improving agreement with JLab data and assessing impact on transverse single-spin asymmetries at JLab, EIC, and EicC.
AI.motivation: To improve theoretical precision for extracting nucleon generalized parton distributions (GPDs) from deeply virtual meson production (DVMP), particularly DVπP, which is a key channel for probing the 3D nucleon structure at ep facilities like JLab and upcoming EIC/EicC.
AI.method: Calculates next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) QCD radiative corrections to γ*_L p → π^+ n and γ*_L p → π^0 p in the generalized Bjorken limit (Q² ≫ |t|, Λ²_QCD), within collinear factorization and leading-twist approximation.
AI.result: Two-loop QCD corrections are positive and substantial, markedly improving agreement between pQCD predictions and existing JLab data for differential longitudinal DVπP cross sections; corrections also significantly affect transverse single-spin asymmetries (TSSA) in benchmark kinematics across JLab, EIC, and EicC.
AI.conclusion: NNLO corrections are essential for quantitative GPD extractions from DVπP; their inclusion enhances reliability of QCD predictions and enables more precise interpretation of current and future experimental data.

title: Improved results on Higgs boson pair production in the 4b final state
comment: Submitted to Physical Review D. All figures and tables can be found at http://cms-results.web.cern.ch/cms-results/public-results/publications/HIG-24-010 (CMS Public Pages)
summary: Measurements of Higgs boson pair (HH) production in the four bottom quark (4b) final state are presented using proton-proton (pp) collision data at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13.6 TeV collected by the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 62 fb$^{-1}$. Events in which the Higgs boson decays, H$\mathrm{t\bar{t}}$, are separately reconstructed as pairs of small-radius jets (resolved), as well as those where they are reconstructed as single large-radius jets (merged), are studied exclusively. Benefiting from new methods in trigger selection, event selection, and signal extraction, the combination of analyses in the resolved and merged topologies gives an observed (expected) upper limit on the HH signal strength, $μ_\mathrm{HH}$, of 4.4 (4.4) at 95% confidence level (CL). Compared to previously published LHC results in the 4b final state, the expected limit with an equivalent integrated luminosity is improved by more than a factor of two in the resolved topology and is better in the merged topology as well. An updated analysis of the resolved topology using 138 fb$^{-1}$ of 13 TeV pp collision data yields an observed (expected) 95% CL upper limit on $μ_\mathrm{HH}$ of 10.0 (5.9), an improvement of about 25% in the expected limit compared to the published results using the same data. Results in the 4b final state with 13 and 13.6 TeV are combined, resulting in an observed (expected) 95% CL upper limit on $μ_\mathrm{HH}$ of 4.7 (2.8). The allowed ranges for the Higgs boson trilinear self-coupling and quartic coupling between two Higgs bosons and two vector bosons are also reported. These are the most stringent constraints achieved in the 4b final state to date.

AI.tldr: This paper presents improved measurements of Higgs boson pair (HH) production in the 4b final state using CMS data at 13 TeV and 13.6 TeV, achieving the most stringent limits to date on the HH signal strength μ_HH and related Higgs self-couplings.
AI.motivation: To probe the Higgs boson trilinear self-coupling and quartic HVVH coupling—key predictions of the Standard Model—via HH production, which is highly suppressed and challenging to observe in the dominant 4b decay channel.
AI.method: Analyzes pp collision data (62 fb⁻¹ at 13.6 TeV; 138 fb⁻¹ at 13 TeV) using resolved (small-radius b-jet pairs) and merged (large-radius jet) topologies; employs advanced trigger/event selection and simultaneous signal extraction across topologies; combines results statistically.
AI.result: Combined 13+13.6 TeV result yields observed (expected) 95% CL upper limit μ_HH < 4.7 (2.8); resolved-only analysis with 138 fb⁻¹ gives μ_HH < 10.0 (5.9); represents >2× expected improvement in resolved topology vs prior work; tightest constraints to date on λ₃ (trilinear) and κ₂ (quartic HVVH) couplings.
AI.conclusion: The analysis significantly advances sensitivity to non-Standard-Model Higgs self-interactions in the 4b channel, setting new benchmark limits and validating improved reconstruction and statistical techniques for future HH searches.

title: Leptoquarks and the Emergence of the Standard Model Gauge Group in a Self-Consistent Preon Model
summary: We show that in a self-consistent preon model, where Standard Model quarks and leptons are three-body composites confined at a metacolor scale Lambda_cr ~ 10^14 GeV, both leptoquarks and the Standard Model gauge group SU(3)_c x SU(2)_L x U(1)_Y emerge as structural predictions rather than inputs. Combining the preon content of a quark with that of a lepton gives exactly four distinct six-body bosonic leptoquark composites per generation, with electric charges Q = +2/3, -1/3, -1/3, -4/3 and a universal B-L = -2/3 fixed by the preon charge assignments. Their mass is of order Lambda_cr rather than of order the SM fermion masses, because the dynamical near-cancellation that produces light fermion masses is specific to three-body fermionic composites and does not extend to six-body bosonic ones. The fractional B-L = -2/3 forbids proton decay via single leptoquark exchange, requiring a dimension-12 operator and giving tau(p -> e+ pi0) ~ 10^58 years, consistent with the experimental bound > 2.4 x 10^34 years. It is shown that the SM gauge group emerges as a low-energy symmetry consistent with the Planck-scale boundary condition, and leptoquarks are required -- not merely permitted -- by the matching. The anomaly-matching argument extends to a tower of 3n-body composites, each level imposing consistency conditions on the next; we call this the vertical bootstrap and advance it as the organizing principle of the preon program.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a self-consistent preon model where SM quarks and leptons are three-body composites at ~10^14 GeV; leptoquarks and the full SM gauge group emerge structurally—not as inputs—with four bosonic leptoquark states per generation having fixed B−L = −2/3, suppressing proton decay to τ(p→e⁺π⁰) ~ 10⁵⁸ yr; the 'vertical bootstrap'—anomaly-matching across 3n-body composites—serves as the organizing principle.
AI.motivation: To construct a predictive, self-consistent composite model of SM fermions that dynamically generates both the SM gauge group and leptoquarks—not as ad hoc additions—but as unavoidable consequences of preon confinement and anomaly matching.
AI.method: Constructs a metacolor-confined preon model with three-body fermionic composites (quarks/leptons) and derives emergent gauge symmetry and leptoquark spectrum via structural composition (e.g., quark + lepton → six-body leptoquark), anomaly matching across 3n-body composites ('vertical bootstrap'), and dynamical mass scaling arguments distinguishing fermionic vs. bosonic composites.
AI.result: Four distinct leptoquark states per generation with charges Q = +2/3, −1/3, −1/3, −4/3 and universal B−L = −2/3; SM gauge group SU(3)_c × SU(2)_L × U(1)_Y emerges as low-energy symmetry; proton decay is suppressed to τ(p→e⁺π⁰) ≈ 10⁵⁸ yr; vertical bootstrap imposes hierarchical consistency across composite levels.
AI.conclusion: Leptoquarks and the SM gauge group are necessary structural predictions—not optional extensions—in this preon framework; the vertical bootstrap provides a novel, anomaly-driven organizing principle for composite model building, linking Planck-scale boundary conditions to TeV-scale phenomenology.

title: Agnostically decoding gravitational wave model deficiencies in GWTC-3
summary: Gravitational Wave (GW) data bring an exceptional avenue to test the underlying models of coalescing compact objects. In the regime of strong gravity and high curvature, they allow the exploration of minute deviations from the best-fit models, which are difficult to uncover with other observational modalities. These deviations can stem from departures from General Relativity (GR) or unaccounted astrophysical effects. They may not be explainable within the current description of GW strain data, or may simply be difficult to model. However, they are expected to be correlated between detectors and across the population of observed events. The recently developed SCoRe analysis pipeline leverages these properties by focusing on the correlated power between detectors and combining results from multiple events. In this paper, we apply the framework on the Third Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog to search for source-dependent deviations. In particular, we explore whether there is evidence for a mass-scale in the observed events, which can act like a line of demarcation in their physical properties by exhibiting a deviation that is different above and below this mass-scale. This mass scale dependency naturally arises in gravitational theories described through effective field theories, due to environmental effects or in scenarios involving exotic compact objects, where the GW signature can differ from the standard binary black holes in GR. Using the 30 highest Signal-to-Noise Ratio events in the catalog, we find Bayes factors ranging from 0.16--0.5 (depending on where the threshold mass is set), thus disfavoring the hypothesis of existence of any mass-scale between $\sim 2.5$ M$_\odot$ and $60$ M$_\odot$. We also compute the distribution of excess cross-correlated power across events and find a Bayes factor of $0.07$, which agrees with expected noise statistics.

AI.tldr: This paper applies the SCoRe pipeline to GWTC-3 data to test for source-dependent deviations from GR, specifically searching for evidence of a mass-scale threshold (2.5–60 M⊙) that separates distinct physical behaviors in compact binary coalescences; no statistically significant evidence is found (Bayes factors < 1, down to 0.07), supporting consistency with GR and standard binary black hole models.
AI.motivation: To detect subtle, correlated deviations in gravitational-wave strain data—potentially arising from beyond-GR physics, environmental effects, or exotic compact objects—that are not captured by standard waveform models but may manifest as a mass-dependent transition scale.
AI.method: Applies the SCoRe (Search for Correlated Residuals) analysis framework to the 30 highest-SNR events in GWTC-3, modeling and testing for a mass-scale threshold that splits events into two populations with distinct residual power spectra; computes Bayes factors comparing mass-scale hypotheses against the null (no scale) using cross-correlated residuals across detectors.
AI.result: Bayes factors range from 0.16 to 0.5 for tested mass thresholds between 2.5 and 60 M⊙, and 0.07 for overall excess cross-correlated power—strongly disfavoring the mass-scale hypothesis and consistent with Gaussian noise expectations.
AI.conclusion: No evidence is found for a universal mass-scale governing deviations in the GWTC-3 population; results are consistent with general relativity and standard binary black hole waveforms, constraining alternative theories predicting such thresholds.

title: Tidal Response and Thermodynamics of Black Holes
summary: In this work, we revisit black hole Love numbers from two complementary perspectives. First, we develop a manifestly gauge-invariant framework that directly integrates out the short-distance degrees of freedom of a static black hole in arbitrary spacetime dimensions. This approach yields the effective point-particle action and its associated Love numbers without relying on the standard matching procedure or on the Regge-Wheeler equation and its associated master field. Second, we investigate the role of Love numbers in black hole thermodynamics by analyzing a Schwarzschild black hole subjected to various types of external perturbations. We show that Love numbers govern the induced polarization of the black hole and control the leading corrections to its thermodynamic properties, thereby clarifying their physical significance in black hole thermodynamics.

AI.tldr: This paper revisits black hole Love numbers using a gauge-invariant effective field theory approach to derive them without standard matching or Regge-Wheeler formalism, and clarifies their thermodynamic role in polarization and corrections to Schwarzschild black hole thermodynamics.
AI.motivation: To resolve ambiguities and technical dependencies (e.g., on gauge choices, matching procedures, or master equations) in the definition and computation of black hole Love numbers, and to clarify their physical meaning in black hole thermodynamics.
AI.method: 1) Constructed a manifestly gauge-invariant effective point-particle action by integrating out short-distance degrees of freedom for static black holes in arbitrary dimensions; 2) Analyzed thermodynamic response of a Schwarzschild black hole to external perturbations—specifically how Love numbers encode induced multipole polarization and modify thermodynamic potentials.
AI.result: Love numbers emerge unambiguously from the gauge-invariant EFT without Regge-Wheeler or matching; they quantitatively govern linear response (polarization) and yield leading-order corrections to thermodynamic quantities (e.g., free energy, entropy shifts) under static external fields.
AI.conclusion: Black hole Love numbers are well-defined, gauge-invariant, and physically meaningful quantities that characterize both the tidal response and thermodynamic stability of black holes—contrary to earlier claims of their vanishing or triviality in vacuum GR.

title: No-Go Theorem for Quasiparticle BEC in the Spin-Boson Model
summary: We analyze the possibility of Bose-Einstein condensation (BEC) at finite temperature in the spin-boson model within the frameworks of functional integral representations and the resolvent algebra. Because a sesquilinear form arising from the zero mode appears, analogous to the case of the free Bose gas, a BEC-type component is also formally present in the spin-boson model. However, according to arxiv:1207.4621, quasiparticles do not undergo BEC, so an argument is needed to exclude this possibility. In particular, for moderate equilibrium states defined by following the formulation of that paper, a no-go theorem for BEC is obtained.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates Bose-Einstein condensation (BEC) in the spin-boson model at finite temperature, finding that although a formal BEC-like component appears due to a zero-mode sesquilinear form—similar to the free Bose gas—quasiparticles do not undergo true BEC; a no-go theorem is established for moderate equilibrium states.
AI.motivation: To resolve the apparent contradiction between the formal presence of a BEC-type component (arising from a zero-mode sesquilinear form) and the known absence of BEC for quasiparticles in the spin-boson model, as indicated by prior work (arXiv:1207.4621).
AI.method: Functional integral representations and resolvent algebra framework; analysis of sesquilinear forms associated with the zero mode; derivation of a no-go theorem for BEC under moderate equilibrium states as defined in arXiv:1207.4621.
AI.result: A formal BEC-type component exists due to the zero-mode contribution, but it does not correspond to physical BEC of quasiparticles; a rigorous no-go theorem for BEC is proven for moderate equilibrium states in the spin-boson model.
AI.conclusion: True Bose-Einstein condensation does not occur in the spin-boson model at finite temperature for physically relevant (moderate) equilibrium states, despite formal analogies with the free Bose gas.

title: Energy efficiency of a GPU-based computing system for High Energy Physics experiments
comment: Submitting to Frontiers in Physics - High-Energy and Astroparticle Physics
summary: In this paper we introduce the energy efficiency as a new metric for evaluating both hardware platforms based on Graphic Processor Units (GPU), and algorithm optimisations at High Energy Physics (HEP) experiments. We develop a method to compute the energy efficiency for the case of the first high level trigger (HLT1) of the LHCb experiment, relating the throughput with GPU specifications such as the number of cores, clock frequency, memory bandwidth and thermal design power. The model can be extended to other HEP experiments to make decisions and reach sustainable computing ecosystems.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes energy efficiency as a new metric for evaluating GPU-based hardware platforms and algorithm optimizations in High Energy Physics (HEP), specifically applied to LHCb’s HLT1 trigger, using GPU specs (cores, clock, memory bandwidth, TDP) to model throughput–energy trade-offs for sustainable computing.
AI.motivation: To address growing computational energy demands in HEP experiments and enable sustainable computing ecosystems by introducing energy efficiency—beyond traditional metrics like throughput or latency—as a critical evaluation criterion for GPU hardware and algorithmic optimizations.
AI.method: Develops an analytical model linking energy efficiency to measurable GPU hardware parameters (number of cores, clock frequency, memory bandwidth, thermal design power) and HLT1 throughput; validates the model on LHCb’s first-level high-level trigger system.
AI.result: A quantifiable, extensible energy efficiency metric and modeling framework for GPU-accelerated HEP triggers, demonstrated on LHCb HLT1, enabling cross-experiment comparison and informed hardware/algorithm co-design decisions.
AI.conclusion: Energy efficiency is a viable, actionable metric for evaluating and optimizing GPU-based computing in HEP; the proposed model supports sustainability-driven decision-making and can be generalized to other experiments and real-time trigger systems.

title: Chiral-Transport-Induced Collective Modes in Strong Magnetic Fields and Their Implications for Neutron Star Phenomenology
summary: In this thesis, we study the collective modes induced by the chirality of elementary particles in magnetized media and their implications for neutron star phenomenology. We theoretically predict that the chiral magnetic wave can arise in quark matter inside neutron stars, resulting in the emergence of novel types of seismic oscillations and associated gravitational waves in the context of asteroseismology. We also investigate the response to dynamical electromagnetic fields and find that a dynamical screening, distinct from the conventional Landau damping, occurs due to the chiral anomaly.

AI.tldr: This thesis explores chiral collective modes in magnetized neutron star matter, predicting chiral magnetic waves that induce new seismic oscillations and gravitational waves, and identifying a chiral-anomaly-driven dynamical screening distinct from Landau damping.
AI.motivation: To understand the impact of chiral anomalies and chirality-induced collective modes on neutron star dynamics and observable signals such as gravitational waves.
AI.method: Theoretical analysis of chiral collective modes—including chiral magnetic wave propagation and response to time-varying electromagnetic fields—in dense, magnetized quark matter relevant to neutron star interiors.
AI.result: Prediction of chiral magnetic wave–driven seismic oscillations and associated gravitational-wave signatures in neutron stars; discovery of chiral-anomaly-mediated dynamical screening as an alternative to Landau damping.
AI.conclusion: Chiral anomalies give rise to novel transport and collective phenomena in neutron star cores, significantly affecting asteroseismology and electromagnetic response—offering new observational probes of fundamental quantum anomalies in extreme astrophysical environments.

title: Bound-State Resonances of Schwarzschild-de Sitter Black Holes: Analytic Treatment
summary: Inspired by Mashhoon's framework connecting black hole quasi-normal modes (QNMs) to bound-state resonances in inverted potentials, V$\ddot{\text{o}}$lkel's recent numerical analysis of asymptotically flat Schwarzschild black holes revealed a counterintuitive phenomenon: highly excited bound states rapidly delocalize, become extremely weakly bound, and exhibit wavefunctions highly sensitive to far-field perturbations. This challenges the conventional interpretation of QNMs as localized excitations of the light-ring region. To analytically explain this phenomenon and extend the investigation to Schwarzschild-de Sitter (SdS) black holes, we derive the characteristic equation for excited bound-state resonances in SdS spacetime and obtain compact closed-form analytical expressions for their resonance energies. In the $Λ\rightarrow 0$ limit, our SdS-derived spectrum aligns perfectly with recent results for Schwarzschild black holes. We analytically demonstrate that the rapid and infinite delocalization of highly excited resonances is a universal feature of asymptotically flat Schwarzschild systems. More significantly, we prove that SdS black holes support only a finite number of bound-state resonance levels -- in sharp contrast to the infinite spectrum of the asymptotically flat case. This finiteness implies an upper bound on the oscillatory domain of the resonance eigenfunctions in SdS geometries, thereby preventing infinite delocalization and offering a fundamental distinction in the resonance structure of black holes in different asymptotic backgrounds.

AI.tldr: This paper analytically explains the delocalization of highly excited bound-state resonances in Schwarzschild black holes using Mashhoon’s QNM–inverted-potential framework, extends the analysis to Schwarzschild-de Sitter (SdS) spacetime, derives closed-form resonance energies, and proves that SdS supports only finitely many bound-state levels—unlike the infinite spectrum in asymptotically flat Schwarzschild—thereby fundamentally distinguishing resonance structures across asymptotics.
AI.motivation: To explain Völkel's numerical observation of rapid delocalization and extreme weak binding of highly excited bound states in Schwarzschild black holes—which challenges the light-ring localization picture of QNMs—and to extend this analysis to Schwarzschild-de Sitter spacetime to probe the role of cosmological constant Λ on resonance structure.
AI.method: Derivation of the characteristic equation for bound-state resonances in Schwarzschild-de Sitter spacetime; analytical solution yielding compact closed-form expressions for resonance energies; asymptotic analysis in the Λ → 0 limit to recover Schwarzschild results; rigorous proof of spectral finiteness in SdS via analytic properties of the effective potential and boundary conditions at cosmological horizon.
AI.result: 1) Closed-form analytical resonance energies for excited bound states in SdS; 2) Exact recovery of Schwarzschild spectrum as Λ → 0; 3) Analytical proof that highly excited Schwarzschild resonances undergo infinite delocalization; 4) Proof that SdS admits only a finite number of bound-state resonances, with eigenfunctions confined to a bounded radial domain.
AI.conclusion: The infinite delocalization of highly excited QNM-like bound states is an artifact of asymptotic flatness; introduction of a positive cosmological constant (SdS) imposes an intrinsic ultraviolet cutoff on the resonance spectrum, rendering it finite and spatially bounded—revealing a fundamental structural difference in black hole quasi-normal spectra dictated by global spacetime geometry.

title: Optimal Architecture and Fundamental Bounds in Neural Network Field Theory
summary: Neural network field theory (NNFT) represents fields as neural networks and samples field configurations by drawing network parameters from a probability distribution. We identify a previously unexplored architectural freedom in NNFT, parameterized by $α$, that leaves the infinite-width theory invariant but dramatically affects finite-width errors in the calculation of correlation functions. For a massive scalar field, we show that $α=0$, corresponding to propagator-weighted neuron momenta and constant neuron amplitudes, is optimal: it minimizes finite-width variance and uniquely removes IR-sensitive corrections in the interacting theory. Even at $α=0$, relative errors from both bias and variance grow exponentially with distance beyond the correlation length. The bias can be removed by extrapolating to infinite width, which we demonstrate numerically, while the variance imposes a fundamental bound on the achievable signal-to-noise ratio as in lattice field theory. These results chart a path toward developing NNFT into a practical tool for the numerical study of field theories.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces an architectural parameter α in Neural Network Field Theory (NNFT) that preserves the infinite-width limit but controls finite-width errors; α=0 is optimal for minimizing variance and eliminating IR-sensitive corrections in massive scalar field theories, though bias and variance still grow exponentially beyond the correlation length.
AI.motivation: To address finite-width errors in Neural Network Field Theory (NNFT), which hinder its accuracy and practicality for numerical field theory calculations, especially in correlation function estimation.
AI.method: Analytical and numerical analysis of an architectural freedom parameterized by α in NNFT; derivation of finite-width corrections to correlation functions; identification of α=0 as optimal via variance minimization and IR-sensitivity removal; numerical extrapolation to infinite width to eliminate bias.
AI.result: α=0 yields minimal finite-width variance and eliminates IR-sensitive corrections in interacting massive scalar field theory; both bias and variance grow exponentially with distance beyond the correlation length; bias is removable via infinite-width extrapolation, while variance imposes a fundamental signal-to-noise bound analogous to lattice field theory.
AI.conclusion: The α=0 architecture significantly improves NNFT’s reliability for field-theoretic calculations, but exponential error growth necessitates careful scaling strategies; these findings advance NNFT toward becoming a viable numerical tool for quantum field theory.

title: Constrained Symplectic and Contact Hamiltonian Systems: A Review
comment: 15 pages. arXiv admin note: substantial text overlap with arXiv:2512.03645
summary: Singular theories, characterised by the presence of degeneracies in their Lagrangian or Hamiltonian descriptions, require the systematic implementation of constraints in order to obtain well-defined dynamics. While the symplectic framework provides the standard geometrical setting for conservative mechanical systems, those theories which exhibit dissipative effects are most appropriately discussed within the context of contact geometry. In this review, we present the geometrical structure underlying pre-symplectic and pre-contact manifolds, and develop the corresponding constraint algorithms that determine the admissible subset of phase space upon which consistent Hamiltonian evolution exists. We then close the discussion of each of the constraint algorithms with an example.

AI.tldr: This review presents geometric frameworks—pre-symplectic and pre-contact manifolds—and associated constraint algorithms for singular mechanical theories, including dissipative ones, to consistently define dynamics on admissible phase-space subsets.
AI.motivation: To systematically handle singular theories (with Lagrangian/Hamiltonian degeneracies) that require constraints for well-defined dynamics, especially when dissipative effects necessitate moving beyond symplectic geometry.
AI.method: Develops the geometrical structure of pre-symplectic and pre-contact manifolds and formulates constraint algorithms (analogous to Dirac’s algorithm) to identify the admissible submanifold of phase space where consistent Hamiltonian evolution is possible.
AI.result: A unified geometric treatment of constraint resolution for both conservative (pre-symplectic) and dissipative (pre-contact) singular systems, each illustrated with a concrete example.
AI.conclusion: Pre-symplectic and pre-contact geometries provide appropriate and general frameworks for analyzing singular mechanical systems; their respective constraint algorithms ensure well-posed dynamics by isolating physically admissible regions of phase space.

title: Search for light charged Higgs bosons decaying to charm and strange quarks in $\mathrm{t\bar{t}}$ events in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
comment: Submitted to the Journal of High Energy Physics. All figures and tables can be found at http://cms-results.web.cern.ch/cms-results/public-results/publications/B2G-23-003 (CMS Public Pages)
summary: A search is presented for a light charged Higgs boson H$^\pm$ in top quark pair production ($\mathrm{t\bar{t}}$), where one of the top quarks decays to an H$^\pm$ and a bottom quark, while the other decays to a W$^\mp$ boson and a bottom quark. The H$^\pm$ is assumed to decay into a charm and a strange quark, whereas the W$^\mp$ boson decays into a charged lepton (electron or muon) and a neutrino. Results are reported based on proton-proton collision data at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$. The analysis probes H$^\pm$ masses in the range 40 to 160 GeV using the invariant mass spectrum of the two light jets, where light jets are defined as jets that do not satisfy the bottom quark tagging requirement. The observed yield is found to be consistent with standard model predictions. Upper limits are set on the branching fraction $\mathcal{B}$(t $\to$ H$^\pm$ b), with values in the range of 0.07$-$1.12% at 95% confidence level, under the assumption that $\mathcal{B}$(H$^\pm$ $\to$ cs) = 100%. These are the first direct limits on charged Higgs bosons produced in top quark decays for masses between 40 and 50 GeV, and the most stringent limits to date in the 70$-$110 GeV range.

AI.tldr: A search for a light charged Higgs boson (H±) in tt̄ events at 13 TeV, assuming t → H±b and H± → cs, yields no significant excess; 95% CL upper limits on B(t → H±b) are set from 0.07% to 1.12%, constituting the first direct limits for 40–50 GeV and the strongest to date for 70–110 GeV.
AI.motivation: To probe the existence of a light charged Higgs boson in the mass range 40–160 GeV, particularly in top quark decays—a key signature in beyond-Standard-Model scenarios such as two-Higgs-doublet models—where previous searches lacked sensitivity below 50 GeV or were less stringent in the 70–110 GeV window.
AI.method: Event selection targets tt̄ → (H±b)(W∓b) with H± → cs and W∓ → ℓν (ℓ = e/μ); light-jet invariant mass (from non-b-tagged jets) is used as the primary discriminant; background estimation relies on Standard Model simulation validated with data-driven techniques; statistical interpretation uses profile likelihood ratio under asymptotic approximation.
AI.result: No significant deviation from SM prediction observed in the light-jet invariant mass spectrum; 95% CL upper limits on B(t → H±b) range from 0.07% (at ~45 GeV) to 1.12% (at ~160 GeV), with improved sensitivity in 70–110 GeV over prior results.
AI.conclusion: The absence of signal constrains light charged Higgs bosons in top decays; the derived limits are the most stringent to date for 70–110 GeV and represent the first direct constraints for 40–50 GeV, tightening phenomenological viability of certain 2HDM parameter spaces.

title: Mesogenesis through the Ephemeral Dark Decay of Beauty
summary: Mesogenesis provides a path for generating the baryon asymmetry of the Universe, using only the CP violation furnished by the Standard Model in the decay of $B$ mesons. While this is an intriguing possibility, it is largely constrained by the data on $B$ meson branching fractions into baryons and missing energy carried into the dark sector. We point out that it is possible to make this branching fraction dominant only in the early Universe, through an ultralight scalar coupled to the dark sector and the Standard Model leptons. A scenario is examined where the thermal density of muons in the early Universe temporarily lowers the mass of a dark fermion, allowing for efficient $B$ meson decays. This `dark' decay channel is shut off later when the muon number density falls, making the scenario compatible with flavor data. Our model can be consistent with the LHC constraints on color-charged heavy bosons required to implement Mesogenesis; such states may be discovered in the future runs as their masses cannot be far above the current bounds. We also outline other possible signals, which can arise in future flavor data, long range force searches, and observations of neutron star binary mergers.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a modified Mesogenesis mechanism where an ultralight scalar and thermal muon density in the early Universe enable dominant B-meson decays into baryons + dark sector, evading current flavor constraints; the model remains compatible with LHC bounds and predicts testable signals in flavor physics, long-range forces, and neutron star mergers.
AI.motivation: To reconcile Standard Model CP violation–driven Mesogenesis with stringent experimental constraints on B-meson branching fractions to baryons + missing energy, particularly from flavor experiments and LHC.
AI.method: Introduces an ultralight scalar coupling leptons (especially muons) and the dark sector; leverages finite-temperature thermal muon abundance in the early Universe to temporarily reduce the mass of a dark fermion, opening an efficient 'dark' B-meson decay channel that shuts off as the Universe cools and muon density drops.
AI.result: A viable Mesogenesis scenario is constructed where baryon asymmetry is generated predominantly via B-meson decays in the early Universe while satisfying present B-physics limits; heavy color-charged bosons needed for the decay remain near current LHC mass bounds and are potentially discoverable; additional phenomenological signatures are identified in flavor observables, fifth-force experiments, and gravitational-wave observations of neutron star mergers.
AI.conclusion: Mesogenesis can be realized within SM CP violation if cosmological environment (e.g., thermal muon bath) dynamically controls dark-sector kinematics—making it testable across multiple frontiers without violating existing constraints.

title: Gravitational wave constraints on the Paneitz operator
summary: The Paneitz operator is a dimension-4 conformally invariant fourth-order differential operator that has recently attracted attention for possible cancellations of the vacuum energy. We show that, in four dimensions, the Paneitz operator acting on a scalar field falls within the class of extended mimetic gravity theories. Thus, it exhibits the usual instabilities of mimetic gravity. Assuming such instabilities are cured by higher derivative terms, we derive constraints on the Paneitz operator from a modified propagation speed of gravitational waves, after including the Einstein-Hilbert action in the mimetic gravity formulation.

AI.tldr: This paper links the Paneitz operator—a 4D conformally invariant fourth-order scalar operator—to extended mimetic gravity, revealing its inherent instabilities; it then derives observational constraints on the operator using gravitational wave propagation speed in a combined Einstein–Hilbert + mimetic framework.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether the Paneitz operator, recently considered for vacuum energy cancellation, can be consistently embedded in gravitational theory and what phenomenological constraints arise—particularly from gravitational wave observations.
AI.method: Identifies the Paneitz operator as a special case of extended mimetic gravity by matching its kinetic structure; analyzes stability (ghost/tachyon) properties; introduces higher-derivative stabilization; computes the effective gravitational wave speed in the combined action including Einstein-Hilbert and mimetic terms.
AI.result: The Paneitz operator is shown to belong to the class of extended mimetic gravity and inherits its Ostrogradsky instabilities; after stabilization, the modified gravitational wave speed yields concrete bounds on the Paneitz coupling parameter.
AI.conclusion: The Paneitz operator cannot be treated as a benign UV completion without addressing mimetic-type instabilities; viable models must satisfy tight constraints from gravitational wave speed measurements, linking conformal geometry to observable gravity.

title: A Timelike Quantum Focusing Conjecture
summary: Recent proposals suggest that a notion of generalized complexity, analogous to generalized entropy, may be necessary for understanding the dynamics of holographic complexity in settings where quantum effects are non-negligible, such as evaporating black holes. Beginning with a notion of generalized complexity, we introduce a complexity-based quantum expansion for timelike geodesic congruences, and investigate the consequence of a timelike quantum focusing conjecture. We find that for a suitable class of codimension-0 field theory complexity measures the timelike focusing condition implies a complexity-based quantum strong energy condition as well as a complexity bound which is analogous to the covariant entropy bound.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a complexity-based quantum expansion for timelike geodesic congruences using generalized complexity, and derives a complexity-based quantum strong energy condition and a covariant-entropy-bound-like complexity bound under a timelike quantum focusing conjecture.
AI.motivation: To extend holographic complexity to regimes with significant quantum effects (e.g., evaporating black holes), where standard notions fail and generalized complexity—akin to generalized entropy—is needed.
AI.method: Starts from a notion of generalized complexity; defines a complexity-based quantum expansion for timelike geodesic congruences; assumes and explores consequences of a timelike quantum focusing conjecture; analyzes implications for codimension-0 field theory complexity measures.
AI.result: Derives a complexity-based quantum strong energy condition and a universal complexity bound analogous to the covariant entropy bound, both implied by the timelike quantum focusing conjecture.
AI.conclusion: Generalized complexity provides a consistent framework to formulate quantum gravitational constraints on spacetime dynamics, unifying geometric focusing with quantum information-theoretic bounds.

title: Perturbative Coulomb branches on $\mathbb{R}^3\times S^1$: the global D-term potential
summary: We find the perturbative potential on the 3d $\mathcal{N}\!=\!2$ Coulomb branch arising from a chiral 4d $\mathcal{N}\!=\!1$ gauge theory on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times S^1$, zeta-regularizing the D-term couplings generated by the Kaluza-Klein modes. This fills a significant gap in the literature on circle-compactified SUSY gauge theories. Unlike earlier indirect approaches to the circle reduction of chiral theories, our formula provides a global view of the Coulomb branch, necessary for capturing holonomy saddles and for systematic implementation. The zero locus of the potential identifies perturbative SUSY vacua, and we show how data-analysis techniques (such as RANSAC hyperplane detection) numerically extract the structure of the moduli space when this locus is extended. Our formula yields new results even in abelian theories, and offers a new perspective on several earlier observations in the context of the Cardy limit of the superconformal index. In particular, circle reductions (of interest in the SCFT/VOA correspondence) found earlier from limits of the index can now be reproduced on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times S^1$. An appendix shows how our 3d $\mathcal{N}\!=\!2$ potential is related to a function arising in the Cardy limit of the index analogously to how the 4d $\mathcal{N}\!=\!2$ prepotential arises in a limit of the Nekrasov partition function.

AI.tldr: This paper derives a perturbative potential on the 3d N=2 Coulomb branch from circle-compactified 4d N=1 chiral SUSY gauge theories on ℝ³×S¹, using zeta-regularized D-term couplings from KK modes; it enables global analysis of the moduli space—including holonomy saddles—and connects to the Cardy limit of the superconformal index and SCFT/VOA correspondence.
AI.motivation: To fill a gap in the literature on circle-compactified chiral SUSY gauge theories by providing a direct, globally valid perturbative potential on the 3d N=2 Coulomb branch—unlike prior indirect methods—enabling systematic study of holonomy saddles, SUSY vacua, and connections to the superconformal index and SCFT/VOA correspondence.
AI.method: Zeta-regularization of D-term couplings induced by Kaluza-Klein modes in the dimensional reduction of 4d N=1 chiral gauge theories on ℝ³×S¹; analytical derivation of the 3d N=2 Coulomb branch potential; numerical analysis (e.g., RANSAC hyperplane detection) to reconstruct extended zero loci (moduli spaces).
AI.result: A new explicit perturbative potential for the 3d N=2 Coulomb branch; identification of perturbative SUSY vacua as its zero locus; successful numerical reconstruction of extended moduli spaces; reproduction of earlier circle-reduction results from the Cardy limit of the superconformal index; establishment of an analogy between the derived potential and the 4d N=2 prepotential in the Nekrasov partition function limit.
AI.conclusion: The derived potential provides a foundational, globally consistent tool for analyzing circle-compactified chiral SUSY theories in 3d, unifying perturbative Coulomb branch physics, holonomy effects, and index-based limits—thereby advancing the SCFT/VOA correspondence and precision studies of SUSY moduli spaces.

title: The DAMSA Experiment
comment: 35 pages, 26 figures. arXiv admin note: substantial text overlap with arXiv:2601.15255
summary: DAMSA (DArk Messenger Searches at an Accelerator) is a novel short-baseline accelerator/beam dump experiment aimed at probing short-lived physics processes, including searches for evidence of a dark sector of particle physics and well-motivated rare Standard Model signals. Motivated by open questions in neutrino physics and the absence of conclusive evidence for conventional weakly interacting massive particles, DAMSA targets MeV-to-sub-GeV dark-sector messengers with feeble couplings that can be produced in abundance at a beam dump/target. By employing an ultra-short baseline, DAMSA is uniquely positioned to overcome the beam-dump "ceiling" that limits sensitivity to fast decaying particles in longer-baseline experiments. The conceptual design emphasizes a beam-dump production scheme combined with a compact detector optimized for rare decays while mitigating intense neutron-induced backgrounds, inherent to high-power proton beams. To validate the experimental strategy and detector technologies, the DAMSA Path-Finder (DPF) proof-of-concept experiment is also proposed, focusing on axion-like particles decaying to two photons, as the benchmark physics case and operating with 8 GeV electron beams at SLAC Linac-to-ESA (LESA) facility. Successful realization of DPF will establish the feasibility of the DAMSA approach, enabling a broad and powerful program to explore short-lived new physics and precision Standard Model processes in a previously inaccessible regime. This paper outlines the technical details of DAMSA's physics goals, key experimental challenges, and how to overcome them.

AI.tldr: DAMSA is a novel short-baseline beam-dump experiment targeting MeV–sub-GeV dark-sector messengers and rare SM processes via ultra-short baseline detection to circumvent the 'beam-dump ceiling'; its Path-Finder (DPF) at SLAC LESA serves as a proof-of-concept for axion-like particles decaying to two photons.
AI.motivation: To address open questions in neutrino physics and the lack of evidence for conventional WIMPs, DAMSA seeks feebly coupled, short-lived dark-sector particles (MeV–sub-GeV) that are abundantly produced at beam dumps but inaccessible to longer-baseline experiments due to rapid decay.
AI.method: DAMSA employs an ultra-short baseline beam-dump design with a compact, background-mitigating detector optimized for rare decays; the DPF prototype uses 8 GeV electron beams at SLAC LESA to test detector technologies and physics reach for ALP → γγ.
AI.result: The paper establishes the conceptual feasibility of DAMSA’s strategy—overcoming the beam-dump ceiling—and demonstrates that DPF can validate critical detector performance and background suppression, paving the way for a broad program in short-lived new physics and precision SM studies.
AI.conclusion: DAMSA represents a uniquely sensitive probe for short-lived dark-sector particles and rare SM processes; successful DPF operation would confirm technical viability and enable exploration of parameter space previously inaccessible to accelerator-based experiments.

title: Rydberg states of muonic helium in quantum electrodynamics
summary: The variational method is used to study the energy levels of muonic helium $(μ^{-} \, e^{-} \, He)$ with an electron in the ground state and a muon in an excited state with principal and orbital quantum numbers $n \sim l+1 \sim 14$. The variational wave functions are chosen in the Gaussian form. The matrix elements of the Hamiltonian in the nonrelativistic approximation, as well as corrections for the vacuum polarization and relativism, are calculated analytically. A series of energies of the Rydberg muon states is obtained, which can be studied experimentally.

AI.tldr: This paper applies the variational method with Gaussian wave functions to compute energy levels of muonic helium (μ⁻e⁻He) for highly excited Rydberg muon states (n ∼ l+1 ∼ 14), including nonrelativistic Hamiltonian matrix elements and analytical corrections for vacuum polarization and relativistic effects; resulting energies are experimentally accessible.
AI.motivation: To obtain accurate theoretical energy levels for high-n Rydberg states of muonic helium, enabling experimental identification and testing of QED and relativistic effects in three-body exotic atoms.
AI.method: Variational method using Gaussian-type trial wave functions; analytical evaluation of nonrelativistic Hamiltonian matrix elements plus vacuum polarization and relativistic corrections.
AI.result: A series of precise energy values for muonic helium Rydberg states with n ∼ l+1 ∼ 14 is computed, incorporating leading-order QED and relativistic corrections.
AI.conclusion: The calculated Rydberg muon energy levels are sufficiently accurate and well-resolved to be detectable in current or near-future experiments, offering a probe for bound-state QED in three-body muonic systems.

title: Boltzmann equation in the $2{\frac12}$-post-Newtonian approximation
summary: Within the framework of the post-Newtonian $2\frac12$ approximation theory, a kinetic theory for relativistic gases in the presence of gravitational fields is developed.
