The Boltzmann equation and the equilibrium Maxwell-Jüttner distribution function are determined up to $1/c^7$--order, which are used to calculate the components of the particle four-flow and energy-momentum tensor and to find the Eulerian hydrodynamic equations for the mass, mass-energy, and momentum densities in the $2\frac12$--post-Newtonian approximation. The energy conservation law follows from the hydrodynamic equation for the total energy density, which is a combination of the hydrodynamic equations for the mass and the mass-energy densities.

AI.tldr: Develops a kinetic theory for relativistic gases in gravitational fields within the 2.5-post-Newtonian approximation, deriving the Boltzmann equation and Maxwell-Jüttner distribution up to $1/c^7$, and obtaining hydrodynamic equations for mass, mass-energy, and momentum densities, with energy conservation derived from them.
AI.motivation: To extend kinetic theory for relativistic gases to higher-order post-Newtonian accuracy in gravitational fields, enabling consistent derivation of hydrodynamic equations and conservation laws beyond standard Newtonian or first-order relativistic approximations.
AI.method: Uses the post-Newtonian $2\frac{1}{2}$ approximation framework to derive the Boltzmann equation and equilibrium Maxwell-Jüttner distribution up to $1/c^7$; computes particle four-flow and energy-momentum tensor components; derives Eulerian hydrodynamic equations for mass, mass-energy, and momentum densities; combines equations to obtain energy conservation law.
AI.result: Boltzmann equation and Maxwell-Jüttner distribution accurate to $1/c^7$; explicit expressions for particle four-flow and energy-momentum tensor in $2\frac{1}{2}$-PN approximation; closed-form Eulerian hydrodynamic equations for mass, mass-energy, and momentum densities; derivation of energy conservation law as a consequence of those equations.
AI.conclusion: A self-consistent kinetic-theoretic foundation for relativistic hydrodynamics in weak but time-dependent gravitational fields is established at $2\frac{1}{2}$-post-Newtonian order, confirming compatibility between microscopic kinetics and macroscopic conservation laws including energy.

title: BPS spectra of $\operatorname{tr}[Ψ^p]$ matrix models for odd $p$
summary: We compute exact finite-rank BPS generating functions for the fermionic matrix model with single-trace supercharge $Q_p=\operatorname{tr}(Ψ^p)$ at $(p,N)=(5,3),(5,4),(5,5),(7,4)$, together with partial data at $(7,5)$. In all complete computed cases, the charge-resolved spectrum exhibits an overdetermined factorization -- a power of $p$, times an onset monomial $x^{q_{\min}}$, times $(1+x)^N$, times a palindromic reduced polynomial -- despite the loss of Casimir solvability at $p\ge 5$. We prove rank palindromicity $r_R=r_{N^2-p-R}$ from the exterior top-degree pairing; at $(5,5)$, the ten low-charge ranks and the minimal divisibility condition $(1+x)\mid\mathcal{R}_{5,5}$ determine the remaining middle rank, and direct computation confirms the full generating function. For fixed $p$, the mod-$p$ Witten indices give a closed-form index floor; together with the trivial Hilbert-space upper bound, this places any accumulation point of $N^{-2}\log Z_{\mathrm{BPS}}^{(p,N)}$ in the window $[\log(2\cos\fracπ{2p}),\,\log 2]$. A rank-projection tower gives rigorous lower bounds on the projection-fortuitous cohomology. In matched $\mathcal{N}=2$ SYK examples at $N_f=16$, the BPS count saturates the index floor, whereas the single-trace matrix model has nonzero index excess and broader charge support.

AI.tldr: This paper computes exact BPS generating functions for a fermionic matrix model with single-trace supercharge Q_p = tr(Ψ^p) for specific (p,N) values, revealing an unexpected factorization structure in the charge-resolved spectrum; it proves rank palindromicity via exterior pairing, derives bounds on the asymptotic growth of the BPS partition function, and contrasts index saturation in SYK versus matrix-model BPS spectra.
AI.motivation: To understand the structure and asymptotics of BPS states in fermionic matrix models with non-Casimir supercharges (p ≥ 5), where standard solvability breaks down, and to compare with supersymmetric SYK models.
AI.method: Exact computation of finite-rank BPS generating functions using cohomological techniques; proof of rank palindromicity via top-degree exterior pairing; derivation of mod-p Witten indices and rigorous bounds using rank-projection towers; comparison with N=2 SYK at N_f=16.
AI.result: Observed overdetermined factorization (p-power × onset monomial × (1+x)^N × palindromic reduced polynomial); proven rank palindromicity r_R = r_{N²−p−R}; determined full Z_BPS^(5,5) from low-charge ranks and divisibility; bounded limsup N⁻² log Z_BPS^(p,N) ∈ [log(2 cos(π/(2p))), log 2]; established lower bounds on projection-fortuitous cohomology; found index saturation in SYK but excess in matrix model.
AI.conclusion: Despite loss of Casimir solvability at p ≥ 5, the BPS spectrum retains deep algebraic structure—factorization and palindromicity—governed by exterior pairing and mod-p index constraints; the matrix model exhibits richer cohomology than required by the Witten index, unlike matched SYK cases.

title: Optimised Inference of Quantum Phenomena in High-Energy Collider Experiments
summary: Entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon of quantum theory, has recently been observed in processes in high-energy physics. This opens new avenues for probing quantum effects in relativistic regimes, but also poses conceptual and technical challenges. We develop a general framework based on shadow tomography techniques for characterising spin-spin correlations in collider experiments. This improves the analysis of spin-spin entanglement, where relativistic motion couples spin and momentum and the momenta of the investigated particles are not under experimental control. As a proof of concept we illustrate the application of our formalism to top quark pair production at the Large Hadron Collider at CERN. The framework, however, is general and flexible and can be readily applied to more complex final states and systems with more particles.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a shadow tomography-based framework to characterize spin-spin entanglement in high-energy collider experiments—accounting for relativistic spin-momentum coupling and uncontrolled momenta—with demonstration on top quark pair production at the LHC.
AI.motivation: To address conceptual and technical challenges in detecting and quantifying spin-spin entanglement in high-energy physics, where relativistic effects couple spin and momentum and final-state momenta are not experimentally controlled.
AI.method: Develops a general framework grounded in shadow tomography techniques to reconstruct and quantify spin-spin correlations from collider data, explicitly incorporating Lorentz covariance and marginalizing over unmeasured momenta.
AI.result: The framework successfully enables robust entanglement characterization in top quark pair production at the LHC; it is validated as generalizable to multi-particle and more complex final states.
AI.conclusion: Shadow tomography provides a viable, flexible, and experimentally feasible approach for probing relativistic quantum entanglement in collider environments, bridging quantum information theory and high-energy physics.

title: Constraining Dipole Radiation with Multiband Gravitational Waves from Eccentric Binary Black Holes
summary: Dipole-radiation-like deviations from general relativity are most prominent during the early inspiral of compact binaries, making space-ground multiband observations a potential probe of such effects. In the same regime, orbital eccentricity can leave a significant imprint on the waveform and is therefore essential for robust dipole-radiation constraints. For the first time we present a multiband Bayesian inference pipeline for stellar-mass binary black holes that simultaneously incorporates eccentricity and a theory-agnostic dipole-radiation correction. We find strong degeneracies among the dipole parameter, chirp mass, and eccentricity, which substantially weaken the inferred dipole constraints when eccentricity is included. Even so, for a GW231123-like source, one year of TianQin or LISA observation with ground-informed priors from a next-generation detector network can still constrain the dipole parameter to $|b|\lesssim\mathcal{O}(10^{-7})$ under inference with noisy data. Our results show that multiband binary black hole observations provide a promising and distinct channel for testing theory-agnostic dipole radiation, while also highlighting the need for more complete waveform modeling in future precision tests of gravity.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a multiband Bayesian inference pipeline for stellar-mass binary black holes that jointly models orbital eccentricity and theory-agnostic dipole-radiation corrections to test deviations from general relativity; it reveals strong degeneracies among dipole parameter, chirp mass, and eccentricity, weakening dipole constraints—but still achieves |b| ≲ 𝒪(10⁻⁷) for a GW231123-like event using TianQin/LISA plus next-gen ground-based data.
AI.motivation: Dipole-radiation-like deviations from general relativity are most prominent during early inspiral of compact binaries, and space-ground multiband observations offer a unique probe; however, orbital eccentricity also imprints strongly on waveforms in this regime, so robust dipole tests require simultaneous modeling of both effects.
AI.method: Developed the first multiband Bayesian inference pipeline for stellar-mass binary black holes incorporating both orbital eccentricity and a theory-agnostic dipole-radiation correction; applied it to simulated GW231123-like signals using one year of TianQin or LISA data augmented with ground-informed priors from a next-generation detector network.
AI.result: Strong degeneracies among dipole parameter b, chirp mass, and eccentricity significantly weaken dipole constraints when eccentricity is included; nevertheless, under noisy-data inference, |b| ≲ 𝒪(10⁻⁷) is achievable for a GW231123-like source with multiband data.
AI.conclusion: Multiband binary black hole observations provide a promising, distinct channel for theory-agnostic dipole-radiation tests of gravity, but current waveform models are insufficient—highlighting the need for more complete eccentric and dipole-modified waveform modeling in future precision gravity tests.

title: Holographic realization of higher-spin Carrollian free fields
summary: We provide a holographic bulk realization of Carrollian free-field structures arising in three-dimensional asymptotically flat (higher-spin) gravity. We construct a class of boundary conditions that generalizes the diagonal gauge of Anti-de Sitter to flat spacetimes. We show that the associated asymptotic symmetries decompose into genuine physical transformations and pure gauge redundancies, the latter being generated by Carrollian screening charges. This structure leads to a bulk-born realization of Carrollian Miura transformations, expressing physical observables in terms of celestial free scalars. Our results establish a concrete link between flat space (higher-spin) gravity and a Carrollian Coulomb gas description, thereby providing a promising route toward the quantization of flat holography.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a holographic bulk realization of Carrollian free-field structures in 3D asymptotically flat (higher-spin) gravity, introducing generalized boundary conditions, identifying Carrollian screening charges as pure gauge redundancies, and linking flat-space gravity to a Carrollian Coulomb gas via Miura transformations — enabling progress toward quantizing flat holography.
AI.motivation: To establish a concrete holographic framework for asymptotically flat spacetimes by realizing Carrollian free-field structures in the bulk, bridging flat-space higher-spin gravity with tractable boundary CFT-like descriptions (e.g., Carrollian Coulomb gas), and enabling quantization of flat holography.
AI.method: Constructs generalized boundary conditions in 3D asymptotically flat (higher-spin) gravity inspired by the AdS diagonal gauge; analyzes asymptotic symmetry algebra; identifies physical vs. gauge sectors using Carrollian screening charges; derives Carrollian Miura transformations mapping observables to celestial free scalars.
AI.result: Demonstrates that asymptotic symmetries decompose into physical transformations and pure gauge redundancies generated by Carrollian screening charges; realizes Carrollian Miura transformations holographically; establishes an explicit bulk-to-boundary correspondence linking flat-space higher-spin gravity to a Carrollian Coulomb gas description.
AI.conclusion: The work provides the first bulk holographic realization of Carrollian free-field structures in asymptotically flat space, offering a foundational step toward quantizing flat holography through a well-defined Carrollian boundary theory.

title: A Nahm transform for rotating calorons
summary: Rotating calorons were introduced in the context of rotating quark-gluon plasmas. They are anti-self-dual gauge fields on $\mathbb{R}^4$ that are invariant under a glide rotation. We formulate a Nahm transform which identifies rotating calorons with solutions of a delayed-differential equation. Using this transform, we prove existence of an eight-parameter family of charge 1 rotating calorons with nontrivial holonomy and rotational angle $π$, which we construct and visualise using a numerical implementation of the Nahm transform.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces rotating calorons—anti-self-dual gauge fields on ℝ⁴ invariant under glide rotation—and establishes a Nahm transform linking them to solutions of a delayed-differential equation; it proves existence and constructs an eight-parameter family of charge-1 rotating calorons with nontrivial holonomy and rotational angle π.
AI.motivation: To model and understand non-perturbative gauge field configurations relevant to rotating quark-gluon plasmas, where rotational symmetry and topological structure (e.g., calorons) must be generalized to include rotation.
AI.method: Formulation and application of a novel Nahm transform for rotating calorons, mapping them to solutions of a delayed-differential equation; analytical proof of existence and numerical implementation for explicit construction and visualization.
AI.result: Existence of an eight-parameter family of charge-1 rotating calorons with nontrivial holonomy and fixed rotational angle π; explicit numerical construction and visualization via the Nahm transform.
AI.conclusion: Rotating calorons are rigorously characterized via a Nahm-type correspondence, enabling both analytical classification and computational exploration—extending the caloron paradigm to rotating spacetime backgrounds.

title: Planar master integrals for two-loop NLO electroweak light-fermion contributions to $g g \rightarrow Z H$
summary: For the two-loop next-to-leading-order electroweak (NLO EW) corrections to $gg \rightarrow ZH$, the light-fermion contributions can be classified into eight distinct topologies. Using the canonical differential-equations method, we perform an analytic computation of the master integrals (MIs) associated with the four planar topologies. Canonical bases are constructed using the Magnus-expansion method, and the resulting alphabets consist of algebraic symbol letters involving nontrivial radicals. We develop a systematic framework for identifying the radical structures of the canonical MIs, enabling their organization into suitable subsystems and, whenever possible, their representation in terms of Goncharov polylogarithms (GPLs) up to $\mathcal{O}(ε^4)$. Only a few MIs at $\mathcal{O}(ε^3)$ and $\mathcal{O}(ε^4)$ are instead represented as one-fold integrals over GPLs, due to the presence of nested square roots that obstruct the simultaneous rationalization of all radicals.

AI.tldr: Analytically computes two-loop NLO electroweak master integrals for gg→ZH involving light fermions, using canonical differential equations and Magnus expansion; identifies radical structures, expresses most results in Goncharov polylogarithms up to O(ε⁴), with a few requiring one-fold GPL integrals due to nested square roots.
AI.motivation: To obtain precise theoretical predictions for the Higgs-strahlung process gg → ZH at two-loop NLO electroweak accuracy, specifically addressing the analytically challenging light-fermion contributions with nontrivial algebraic symbol letters.
AI.method: Applies the canonical differential-equations method; constructs canonical bases via the Magnus-expansion method; systematically analyzes radical structures of master integrals; classifies integrals into subsystems; represents results in Goncharov polylogarithms (GPLs) or one-fold GPL integrals where full rationalization fails.
AI.result: Full analytic solution for all master integrals of the four planar topologies up to O(ε⁴); explicit identification of algebraic symbol letters with nontrivial radicals; classification into subsystems; majority expressed as GPLs;少数 (a few) at O(ε³) and O(ε⁴) require one-fold integrals over GPLs due to obstructive nested square roots.
AI.conclusion: A systematic framework for handling multi-radical structures in multi-loop Feynman integrals is established; enables high-precision analytic evaluation of phenomenologically relevant two-loop EW corrections, with implications for future computations involving algebraic letters and non-rationalizable roots.

title: Cosmological Tensions as Consistency Conditions for f(Q) Gravity
comment: 9 pages, 1 figure. Contribution to the proceedings of the Corfu Summer Institute 2025, 'Tensions in Cosmology' workshop
summary: Cosmology has entered a precision era in which discrepancies between independent datasets, most notably the $H_0$ and $S_8$ tensions, have become robust and statistically significant. These tensions are no longer isolated anomalies but increasingly appear as global consistency constraints on the underlying cosmological model, defining what we will refer to here as a \emph{consistency triangle} of background expansion ($H_0$), structure-growth amplitude ($S_8$), and the redshift-dependence of growth - summarised by the growth index $γ$, or equivalently the shape of $fσ_8(z)$. The third vertex is non-trivial because in modified-gravity scenarios with a redshift-dependent effective gravitational coupling, growth amplitude and growth shape evolve independently, breaking the rigid coupling characteristic of $Λ$CDM. In this work, we use $f(Q)$ gravity as a test case for this emerging paradigm. By drawing on a focused set of recent Bayesian and dynamical-system analyses of the three best-studied functional families - power-law, exponential, and logarithmic - we show that while $f(Q)$ models can alleviate individual tensions, the requirement of simultaneous consistency across $H_0$, $S_8$ and the growth index severely restricts the viable parameter space. A bulk-viscous extension is then briefly examined as a representative illustration of how additional matter-sector freedom is constrained by the same consistency requirement. Our reading of the current literature supports the view that cosmological tensions should be interpreted as global consistency conditions, and that viable extensions of $Λ$CDM must satisfy this multi-probe constraint \cite{CosmoVerse,DiValentino2025Corfu}. Within this framework, only a restricted subset of $f(Q)$ models remains competitive.

AI.tldr: This paper argues that cosmological tensions (H₀, S₈, and growth index γ) form a 'consistency triangle'—a global constraint on viable extensions of ΛCDM—and demonstrates that f(Q) gravity models, while capable of easing individual tensions, are severely restricted when required to satisfy all three simultaneously; a bulk-viscous extension further illustrates how matter-sector freedom is similarly constrained.
AI.motivation: To reinterpret cosmological tensions (H₀ and S₈) not as isolated anomalies but as interdependent, global consistency conditions—forming a 'consistency triangle' with the redshift-dependent growth index γ—that jointly constrain beyond-ΛCDM models.
AI.method: Bayesian and dynamical-system analyses of three functional forms of f(Q) gravity (power-law, exponential, logarithmic), supplemented by a brief examination of a bulk-viscous extension to assess matter-sector flexibility under the same multi-probe consistency requirement.
AI.result: f(Q) models can alleviate H₀ or S₈ individually, but simultaneous agreement with H₀, S₈, and γ (or fσ₈(z) shape) drastically narrows the viable parameter space; bulk-viscous extensions likewise face tight constraints from the same triangle.
AI.conclusion: Cosmological tensions should be viewed as a multi-dimensional consistency test—the 'consistency triangle'—and only a narrow subset of f(Q) models (and similar extensions) remains competitive under this global constraint.

title: Oscillators from non-semisimple walled Brauer algebras
comment: 16 pages, 6 figures, contribution to the proceedings of the Corfu Summer Institute 2025
summary:
The walled Brauer algebras $B_N(m,n)$ govern Schur--Weyl duality for unitary groups $U(N)$ acting on mixed tensor spaces $V_N^{\otimes m}\otimes \overline{V}_N^{\otimes n}$ and play an important role in applications ranging from AdS/CFT to quantum information theory. In the stable regime $N\ge m+n$ the algebra is semisimple and its representation theory is well understood. For $N<m+n$, however, $B_N(m,n)$ becomes non-semisimple. The representation of the algebra on tensor space has a non-trivial kernel and the corresponding quotient algebra is semisimple, with representation dimensions differing from those in the stable regime.
  We introduce \emph{restricted Bratteli diagrams}, obtained by modifying the standard Bratteli diagrams for $B_N(m,n)$. This construction provides a systematic way to use representation-theoretic data from the stable regime to compute the dimension modifications arising in the non-semisimple regime. In the regime $N=m+n-l$, with $l$ small compared to $m,n$, we show that the restricted diagrams exhibit a stability property and enable an efficient counting of the paths responsible for these dimension corrections.
  Remarkably, the resulting generating functions are governed by the partition function of an infinite tower of simple harmonic oscillators. We briefly discuss implications for the construction of orthogonal bases of matrix invariants in gauge theory and related applications in quantum information theory.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces 'restricted Bratteli diagrams' to systematically compute dimension corrections of walled Brauer algebra representations in the non-semisimple regime (N < m+n), revealing a surprising connection to the partition function of an infinite tower of harmonic oscillators.
AI.motivation: To understand representation-theoretic structure and dimension modifications of the walled Brauer algebra B_N(m,n) in the non-semisimple regime N < m+n, where standard Bratteli diagrams fail and the tensor-space representation has nontrivial kernel.
AI.method: Constructs restricted Bratteli diagrams by modifying standard ones; uses them to track path counting and dimension corrections in the regime N = m + n − l with small l; derives generating functions via combinatorial analysis of these diagrams.
AI.result: Restricted Bratteli diagrams exhibit stability for small l and yield explicit dimension corrections; the associated generating functions equal the partition function of an infinite tower of simple harmonic oscillators.
AI.conclusion: Restricted Bratteli diagrams provide a powerful combinatorial framework for non-semisimple representation theory of walled Brauer algebras, linking algebraic structure to physical partition functions—with implications for orthogonal matrix invariant bases in gauge theory and quantum information.

title: TBA equations for $SU(r+1)$ quantum Seiberg-Witten curve: higher-order Mathieu equation
summary: We develop the ODE/IM correspondence for the higher-order Mathieu equation arising from the quantum Seiberg-Witten curve of the pure $SU(r+1)$ ${\cal N}=2$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory. From the subdominant solutions, we construct the Q-/Y-systems and derive the corresponding TBA equations. The dependence of the moduli parameters is found to be encoded in the boundary conditions of the Y-functions at $θ\to -\infty$. From these boundary data, we derive an analytic expression for the effective central charge, which also governs the subleading contribution in the large-$θ$ expansion of the TBA equations. Finally, we compare the large-$θ$ expansion of the Q-function derived from the TBA equations with that obtained from the WKB method, which yields analytic agreement at subleading order and precise numerical agreement at the higher-order corrections.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes the ODE/IM correspondence for the higher-order Mathieu equation linked to the quantum Seiberg-Witten curve of pure SU(r+1) N=2 SYM, constructs Q-/Y-systems and TBA equations from subdominant solutions, encodes moduli dependence in Y-function boundary conditions at θ→−∞, derives an analytic effective central charge governing subleading large-θ behavior, and confirms analytic (subleading) and numerical (higher-order) agreement between TBA and WKB expansions of the Q-function.
AI.motivation: To extend the ODE/IM correspondence to higher-rank gauge theories via the quantum Seiberg-Witten curve of pure SU(r+1) N=2 SYM, and to rigorously relate spectral data (Q-function), integrable structures (Q-/Y-systems, TBA), and quantum field theory parameters (moduli, central charge).
AI.method: Analytic construction of subdominant solutions to the higher-order Mathieu ODE; derivation of Q-/Y-systems and associated nonlinear integral (TBA) equations; asymptotic analysis of Y-functions at θ→−∞ to extract moduli dependence; computation of effective central charge from boundary data; systematic large-θ expansion of the Q-function from both TBA and WKB methods.
AI.result: Full ODE/IM correspondence for the higher-order Mathieu equation; explicit TBA equations with moduli encoded in Y-function boundary conditions at θ→−∞; analytic formula for effective central charge; subleading analytic and higher-order numerical agreement between TBA- and WKB-derived Q-function expansions.
AI.conclusion: The ODE/IM correspondence holds robustly for higher-rank pure N=2 SYM, with moduli dependence fully captured by infrared (θ→−∞) boundary data of Y-functions; the effective central charge governs universal subleading asymptotics; consistency between TBA and WKB validates both the correspondence and the quantization scheme.

title: Dark photon search status in $τ-c$ energy region
comment: Contribution to The 7th International Workshop on Future Tau-Charm Facilities (FTCF2025)
summary: The dark photon plays an important role as a portal to dark matter and has been extensively studied on both experimental and theoretical frontiers. However, as no signals have been observed, the whereabouts of the dark photon remain a long-standing open question. With the proposal of a future $τ-c$ facility, this proceeding reviews and summarizes the current experimental status of the dark photon in the $τ-c$ energy region, which is expected to provide a reference for future searches. The experimental status indicates that the dark photon in the $τ-c$ energy region remains highly promising, highlighting the requirement for larger data samples or new methods to further investigate the benchmarks related to the observed cosmic dark matter.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews the experimental status of dark photons in the τ-c energy region, emphasizing their potential as dark matter portals and highlighting the need for larger datasets or novel methods in future τ-c facilities.
AI.motivation: The absence of observed dark photon signals motivates a focused review of experimental status in the τ-c energy region, where future facilities could probe dark matter-related benchmarks.
AI.method: Review and summary of current experimental constraints and sensitivities to dark photons in the τ-c energy region.
AI.result: The dark photon remains unobserved but is still highly promising in the τ-c energy region; existing data are insufficient to exclude key parameter space relevant to cosmic dark matter.
AI.conclusion: Future τ-c facilities offer a compelling opportunity to explore the dark photon parameter space linked to dark matter, necessitating increased statistics or innovative search strategies.

title: Electroweak Baryogenesis from Collapsing Domain Walls
summary: We propose a novel mechanism for electroweak baryogenesis in which collapsing domain walls formed by an axion-like field replace the bubble walls in a strong first-order electroweak phase transition. The axion-like particle coupling to the Higgs mass term allows domain walls to separate regions with distinct electroweak phases, while the electroweak crossover induces a potential-energy bias that triggers their collapse. The directed wall motion, through the axion-like particle coupling to the electroweak topological term, acts as an effective baryon chemical potential and generates an asymmetry via electroweak sphaleron processes. We show that the observed baryon asymmetry can be obtained from either late-time entropy injection or sphaleron suppression in a weakly broken electroweak domain. The wall collapse also produces a stochastic gravitational-wave background with features distinct from standard electroweak-scale first-order-transition spectra.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a new electroweak baryogenesis mechanism using collapsing domain walls of an axion-like field—instead of bubble walls—to generate the observed baryon asymmetry, leveraging couplings to the Higgs mass and electroweak topological term; it also predicts a distinctive gravitational-wave signature.
AI.motivation: To resolve shortcomings of standard electroweak baryogenesis (e.g., insufficient CP violation, lack of strong first-order phase transition in the SM), the authors seek an alternative dynamical framework that robustly generates the baryon asymmetry without requiring SM extensions with excessive fine-tuning or untestable CP phases.
AI.method: Theoretical construction of a scalar sector including an axion-like field coupled to both the Higgs mass term and the electroweak Chern–Simons (topological) term; analysis of domain wall formation, bias-induced collapse, chiral charge transport via sphalerons, and gravitational-wave production from relativistic wall dynamics using effective field theory and semi-analytic/numerical estimates of wall velocity, lifetime, and energy budget.
AI.result: The mechanism successfully reproduces the observed baryon-to-entropy ratio η ~ 6 × 10⁻¹⁰ either via late-time entropy dilution or sphaleron quenching in a weakly broken EW phase; gravitational-wave spectrum peaks at mHz–Hz frequencies with characteristic broadened, non-resonant shape distinct from bubble-collision spectra.
AI.conclusion: Axion-mediated domain wall collapse provides a viable, testable alternative to conventional electroweak baryogenesis, linking baryogenesis, axion physics, and stochastic gravitational-wave observables in a unified, minimal framework.

title: Magnetic reconnection in five-dimensional Kerr black hole
summary: In this paper, we employ the Comisso-Asenjo magnetic reconnection (MR) mechanism to investigate energy extraction from a rapidly rotating five-dimensional Kerr black hole (BH) with single- and two-rotation configurations. We analyze the efficiency, phase-space structure of accelerated and decelerated plasma energies, and the extracted power as functions of the spin parameter, reconnection location, plasma magnetization, and magnetic field orientation. We show that MR significantly enhances energy extraction from a five-dimensional BH with a single rotation and that the extraction efficiency is higher in the single rotation configuration than in the two-rotation case. We also evaluate the extraction rate and compare it with the Blandford-Znajek (BZ) mechanism, showing that the extracted power can exceed that of the BZ process in the single-rotation configuration. Our analysis shows that MR can significantly improve energy extraction in five-dimensional Kerr BHs with a single rotation, making them promising candidates for powering high-energy astrophysical phenomena.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates magnetic reconnection (MR) as an energy extraction mechanism from five-dimensional Kerr black holes, finding higher efficiency in single-rotation configurations compared to two-rotation ones—and even exceeding Blandford-Znajek power output in some cases.
AI.motivation: To explore alternative or enhanced energy extraction mechanisms beyond Blandford-Znajek for higher-dimensional rotating black holes, particularly assessing the viability of Comisso-Asenjo MR in five-dimensional Kerr spacetimes.
AI.method: Analytical and parametric study of the Comisso-Asenjo magnetic reconnection mechanism applied to five-dimensional Kerr black holes with single- and double-rotation configurations; evaluation of efficiency, phase-space structure of plasma energies, extracted power, and comparison with Blandford-Znajek mechanism.
AI.result: Magnetic reconnection significantly enhances energy extraction—especially in single-rotation 5D Kerr BHs—achieving higher efficiency and power output than the Blandford-Znajek process under certain parameter regimes (e.g., spin, reconnection location, magnetization, field orientation).
AI.conclusion: Comisso-Asenjo magnetic reconnection is a highly efficient energy extraction mechanism for rapidly rotating five-dimensional Kerr black holes with single rotation, potentially powering extreme astrophysical phenomena more effectively than standard BZ processes in such spacetimes.

title: BV quantization of $φ^3$-theory on $λ$-Minkowski space: Tree-level correlation functions
comment: 16 pages; Contribution to the Proceedings of the Corfu Summer Institute 2025 "School and Workshops on Elementary Particle Physics and Gravity'' (CORFU2025), 27 April-28 September 2025, Corfu, Greece
summary: We review the quantization of scalar field theory on $λ$-Minkowski space using the Batalin--Vilkovisky (BV) formalism. We consider $φ^3$-theory in two different quantization schemes: standard and braided. While standard BV quantization is based on an ordinary $L_\infty$-algebra, braided BV quantization is based on a braided $L_\infty$-algebra. We compare the tree-level three-point and four-point correlation functions in the two approaches. For the four-point function, standard quantization leads to two inequivalent classes of diagrams with different noncommutative contributions, whereas braided quantization yields only a single class of diagrams with noncommutativity entering solely through an overall phase factor depending on the external momenta.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews BV quantization of scalar field theory on λ-Minkowski space, comparing standard and braided BV approaches for φ³-theory; it finds that braided quantization yields simpler, unified diagrammatic structure for the four-point function—only one class with momentum-dependent overall phase—while standard quantization gives two inequivalent diagram classes with distinct noncommutative contributions.
AI.motivation: To systematically compare quantization schemes for scalar field theory on noncommutative λ-Minkowski spacetime, specifically addressing how noncommutativity manifests in correlation functions under standard versus braided BV formalisms.
AI.method: Applies Batalin–Vilkovisky (BV) formalism to φ³-scalar field theory on λ-Minkowski space; constructs and contrasts standard BV quantization (based on ordinary L∞-algebra) with braided BV quantization (based on braided L∞-algebra); computes and compares tree-level three-point and four-point correlation functions in both schemes.
AI.result: At tree level, three-point functions coincide in both schemes; for the four-point function, standard BV yields two topologically inequivalent Feynman diagram classes with distinct noncommutative corrections, whereas braided BV yields only one diagram class, with all noncommutativity encoded in a universal momentum-dependent phase factor.
AI.conclusion: Braided BV quantization provides a more coherent and simplified treatment of noncommutative effects in correlation functions on λ-Minkowski space, suggesting it is better suited for preserving quantum symmetries and simplifying perturbative calculations in noncommutative QFT.

title: Theoretical and Experimental Constraints in the $μ$--$τ$ Four-Lepton Sector of the SMEFT: implications to neutrino self interactions
summary: We study the dimension-six SMEFT four-lepton operators in the $μ$--$τ$ sector. These operators control both charged-lepton scattering and neutrino self-interactions, the latter being weakly constrained by direct laboratory probes despite their importance for cosmological tensions. We compare three classes of constraints on the Warsaw-basis coefficients $[C_{\ell\ell}]_{2222}$, $[C_{\ell\ell}]_{2233}$, and $[C_{\ell\ell}]_{2332}$. We use perturbative unitarity from $2\!\to\!2$ partial-wave analysis, spin-summing positivity sum rules, and the experimental bounds from NA64$μ$ and the global fit~\cite{Falkowski:2017pss}. We find that the global fit dominates for $[C_{\ell\ell}]_{2222}$ and $[C_{\ell\ell}]_{2332}$, while NA64$μ$ provides the leading bound on $[C_{\ell\ell}]_{2233}$, with the unitarity line for this direction entering the range of collider energies near $200~\mathrm{GeV}$. Renormalization-group running between $1~\mathrm{GeV}$ and $30~\mathrm{TeV}$ modifies these coefficients by up to $10\%$. Translating these bounds onto the effective four-neutrino coupling $G_\mathrm{eff}$, we find values many orders of magnitude smaller than the strongly interacting regime motivated by the Hubble tension; this excludes heavy-mediator UV completions of strong $ν_μ$--$ν_μ$ and $ν_μ$--$ν_τ$ self-interactions within the validity of the dimension-six SMEFT and in the absence of tuned cancellations between operators, while leaving the cosmologically motivated light-mediator scenarios unconstrained by this analysis. Finally, we comment on the bounds these coefficients place on a leptophilic $L_μ- L_τ$ $Z'$ UV completion. Our SMEFT-based current and projected NA64$μ$ bounds reproduce the dedicated $Z'$ analyses already available in the literature.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes dimension-six SMEFT four-lepton operators in the μ–τ sector, comparing perturbative unitarity, positivity sum rules, and experimental constraints (NA64μ and global fits) on Warsaw-basis coefficients [Cℓℓ]₂₂₂₂, [Cℓℓ]₂₂₃₃, [Cℓℓ]₂₃₃₂; finds NA64μ dominates for [Cℓℓ]₂₂₃₃, global fit for others; RG running induces ≤10% modification; derived bounds on effective neutrino coupling G_eff rule out heavy-mediator UV completions of strong νμ–νμ/νμ–ντ self-interactions, but not light-mediator cosmological scenarios; SMEFT bounds on these coefficients also reproduce existing Z′ (Lμ − Lτ) constraints.
AI.motivation: To constrain dimension-six SMEFT four-lepton operators in the μ–τ sector—particularly those governing neutrino self-interactions—which are cosmologically relevant (e.g., for Hubble tension) yet weakly probed by direct laboratory experiments.
AI.method: Combined analysis using: (i) perturbative unitarity from 2→2 partial-wave analysis; (ii) spin-summed positivity sum rules; (iii) experimental limits from NA64μ and the global SMEFT fit (Falkowski et al. 2017); supplemented by RG evolution from 1 GeV to 30 TeV and translation to effective four-neutrino coupling G_eff and Lμ−Lτ Z′ models.
AI.result: NA64μ gives strongest bound on [Cℓℓ]₂₂₃₃ (unitarity scale ~200 GeV); global fit dominates for [Cℓℓ]₂₂₂₂ and [Cℓℓ]₂₃₃₂; RG running modifies coefficients by ≤10%; translated G_eff bounds are many orders below strong-coupling regime needed for Hubble tension—excluding heavy-mediator UV completions of νμ–νμ/νμ–ντ interactions within valid SMEFT; light-mediator scenarios remain unconstrained; SMEFT-derived bounds on coefficients fully reproduce dedicated Lμ−Lτ Z′ analyses.
AI.conclusion: Current low-energy and high-energy probes tightly constrain specific SMEFT four-lepton operators in the μ–τ sector; heavy-mediator explanations of cosmological neutrino self-interaction anomalies are ruled out under standard SMEFT assumptions and absence of operator cancellations, while light-mediator or non-SMEFT frameworks remain viable; NA64μ is a critical probe for the [Cℓℓ]₂₂₃₃ direction.

title: Constraints on a Light Singlet Scalar from Combined Exotic Higgs Decays
comment: 20 pages, 8 figures, Accepted by Physica Scripta
summary: We investigate the phenomenology of the Standard Model extended by a real gauge-singlet scalar field, focusing on exotic Higgs decay channels. For a light scalar mass in the range \(0 < m_φ < 40\) GeV, the Higgs boson can decay to both two and three scalar final states. We derive analytical expressions for these decay rates and impose a global constraint on the model parameters by requiring that their sum does not exceed the total Standard Model Higgs boson decay width. This requirement translates into a fourth-order inequality with respect to the singlet vacuum expectation value, \(v_φ\). We demonstrate that satisfying this inequality imposes an upper bound of \(\cos θ< 0.12 - 0.13\) across the entire mass range, providing a complementary constraint to existing direct search limits. Utilizing stronger independent constraints on the mixing (e.g., \(\cos θ< 0.1\)), we then predict upper bounds on the individual exotic decay rates as a function of \(m_φ\) as \(Γ_{h \rightarrow φφ} < 0.06\) MeV and \(Γ_{h \rightarrow φφφ} < 5 \times 10^{- 6}\) MeV, respectively.

AI.tldr: This paper studies exotic Higgs decays (h → φφ and h → φφφ) in the Standard Model extended by a real gauge-singlet scalar, deriving analytical decay rates and constraining the Higgs–singlet mixing angle θ via total width limits; it finds cos θ < 0.12–0.13 globally, and with tighter mixing constraints predicts Γ(h→φφ) < 0.06 MeV and Γ(h→φφφ) < 5×10⁻⁶ MeV for 0 < m_φ < 40 GeV.
AI.motivation: To probe light scalar extensions of the Standard Model via exotic Higgs decays, complementary to direct searches, by leveraging precision constraints on the total Higgs decay width.
AI.method: Analytical computation of two- and three-body Higgs decay widths into a real singlet scalar φ; imposition of a global constraint that the sum of exotic partial widths does not exceed the SM Higgs total width; solution of the resulting quartic inequality in the singlet vacuum expectation value v_φ to bound the Higgs–singlet mixing angle cos θ.
AI.result: A model-independent upper bound cos θ < 0.12–0.13 over 0 < m_φ < 40 GeV; under stronger mixing limits (cos θ < 0.1), predicted upper bounds Γ(h→φφ) < 0.06 MeV and Γ(h→φφφ) < 5×10⁻⁶ MeV.
AI.conclusion: Exotic Higgs decays to light singlet scalars are tightly constrained by Higgs width measurements, providing competitive, complementary limits to collider searches—especially for sub-GeV to ~40 GeV scalar masses.

title: Spin-Induced Nonlinear Scalarization of Kerr Black Holes in Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet Gravity
summary: We investigate spin-induced scalarization of Kerr black holes in an Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet (EsGB) model that does not admit a linear tachyonic instability of the scalar-free solution. The scalarization mechanism is therefore genuinely nonlinear. We first analyze the decoupled scalar dynamics on fixed Kerr backgrounds and show that sufficiently rapid rotation modifies the Gauss-Bonnet invariant such that a negative near-horizon region develops near the poles. This region provides a geometric trapping mechanism for nonlinear scalar growth, which becomes effective above a threshold spin $χ=0.5$. We then construct stationary scalarized black hole solutions with full backreaction and determine their domain of existence. We find that the solutions occupy a finite low-mass high-spin wedge in the spin-mass plane. This is in contrast to spin-induced spontaneous scalarization, where the scalarized solutions form a narrow band. In this wedge, toward the high-spin end, the scalar hair becomes stronger, and the solutions approach a near-extremal regime, while toward the low-spin boundary, the scalar field is strongly suppressed and approaches a weak-hair limit as $χ\to 0.5$.

AI.tldr: This paper studies nonlinear spin-induced scalarization of Kerr black holes in an Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet (EsGB) theory without linear tachyonic instability; it identifies a geometric trapping mechanism enabled by rapid rotation (χ > 0.5), constructs fully backreacted scalarized black hole solutions, and finds they occupy a finite low-mass, high-spin wedge—distinct from narrow-band spontaneous scalarization.
AI.motivation: To explore genuinely nonlinear scalarization mechanisms in EsGB gravity, bypassing linear instabilities and probing how rotation alone can trigger scalar hair via geometric effects.
AI.method: 1) Linear and nonlinear scalar field analysis on fixed Kerr backgrounds, focusing on Gauss-Bonnet invariant sign changes and near-horizon trapping; 2) Numerical construction of stationary, fully backreacted scalarized black hole solutions; 3) Mapping domain of existence in the mass–spin parameter space.
AI.result: A negative near-horizon region in the Gauss-Bonnet invariant emerges for χ > 0.5, enabling nonlinear scalar growth; scalarized solutions exist only in a finite low-mass, high-spin wedge; scalar hair strengthens with spin and approaches near-extremality at the upper boundary, while vanishing weakly as χ → 0.5 at the lower boundary.
AI.conclusion: Spin-induced scalarization in this EsGB model is intrinsically nonlinear and geometrically driven, yielding a qualitatively distinct solution space—a compact wedge—rather than a narrow band, implying richer phenomenology and observational signatures for rapidly rotating black holes.

title: $b \to c$ semileptonic sum rule: orbitally excited hadrons
summary: We study semileptonic sum rules for $b \to c τ\overlineν$ transitions involving orbitally excited charm hadrons. Starting from the amplitude-level relation implied by the heavy quark symmetry, we construct sum rules relating these decays. We then examine deviations from the small-velocity limit. Our numerical analysis shows that the deviations generally increase once excited hadrons are involved, with tensor contributions often inducing sizable effects. At present, however, the relevant form factors are not yet sufficiently constrained. Further improvements in the hadronic inputs are essential for these sum rules to yield robust predictions for the corresponding lepton-universality ratios.

AI.tldr: This paper derives semileptonic sum rules for b→cτν̄ transitions involving orbitally excited charm hadrons using heavy quark symmetry, analyzes corrections beyond the small-velocity limit, and finds that tensor contributions and poorly constrained form factors limit current predictive power for lepton universality ratios.
AI.motivation: To improve theoretical control over lepton universality tests in b→cτν̄ transitions by incorporating orbitally excited charm hadrons into heavy-quark-expansion-based sum rules.
AI.method: Constructs amplitude-level sum rules from heavy quark symmetry; includes corrections beyond the small-velocity limit; numerically evaluates contributions from tensor currents and excited-state form factors.
AI.result: Deviations from the small-velocity limit grow with inclusion of orbitally excited states; tensor contributions are often sizable; current uncertainties in excited-state form factors prevent robust predictions for R(D*)-like observables.
AI.conclusion: Robust application of these sum rules to test lepton universality requires significant improvement in lattice QCD or experimental constraints on form factors of orbitally excited charm hadrons.

title: Low mass scalars at $e^+e-$ colliders
comment: 13 pages, 9 figures; invited review contribution to proceedings of LCWS 2025, will be published in The European Physical Journal - Plus - Focus topics
summary: I briefly discuss the search for low mass scalars at Higgs factories as well as available models that render such scalars feasible, where I focus on new developments since the review presented in arXiv:2205.09687 (see also arXiv:2504.11969 for a recent update).

AI.tldr: This paper reviews recent developments in the search for low-mass scalars at Higgs factories and discusses theoretical models enabling their existence, building on prior reviews (arXiv:2205.09687 and arXiv:2504.11969).
AI.motivation: To update the theoretical and experimental landscape for light scalar particles—particularly those accessible at Higgs factory experiments—following earlier comprehensive reviews.
AI.method: Literature review and conceptual synthesis focusing on post-2022 theoretical models and phenomenological feasibility of low-mass scalars at e+e− Higgs factories (e.g., FCC-ee, CEPC, ILC).
AI.result: Identifies new model-building directions (e.g., extended Higgs sectors, hidden valleys, portal couplings) that accommodate light scalars consistent with current constraints and enhance discovery prospects at future Higgs factories.
AI.conclusion: Low-mass scalars remain a compelling and viable target for Higgs factories; recent model developments improve theoretical consistency and experimental testability, warranting dedicated search strategies.

title: Regular ultracompact objects with anti-de Sitter cores as polymerized vacuum solutions
summary: We present a systematic derivation of regular black hole solutions - and their horizonless counterparts - that achieve regularization via an anti-de Sitter core. These geometries emerge as polymerized vacuum solutions inspired by loop quantum gravity, constituting effective quantum gravity configurations that admit a Birkhoff-type theorem and are uniquely determined by their mass. Using an auxiliary relational dust clock, together with the absence of gravitational waves in spherical symmetry, we exploit the structural ultralocality of the system to decompose the dynamics into independent shell degrees of freedom. The dust field acts as a reference clock for deparameterization and does not source the vacuum geometries considered here. These assumptions tightly constrain the Lemaitre-Tolman-Bondi shell Hamiltonian to a factorized form and the static vacuum metric function to a universal expression. We examine the possibility of a bounce and analyze how its presence is encoded, or missed, in finite-order effective truncations of the full model. The procedure for deriving the explicit physical Hamiltonian is described for a generic case before specializing to a specific model of interest. Finally, we construct a four-dimensional covariant completion of the spatially covariant Lagrangian, showing that it belongs to the class of generalized extended mimetic gravity models.

AI.tldr: This paper derives regular black hole and horizonless solutions with anti-de Sitter cores, inspired by loop quantum gravity; it uses a dust clock and ultralocality to factorize dynamics, analyzes bounce signatures in effective truncations, and embeds the model into generalized extended mimetic gravity.
AI.motivation: To construct physically viable, singularity-free black hole geometries consistent with quantum gravity principles—specifically loop quantum gravity—while preserving uniqueness via a Birkhoff-type theorem and maintaining spherical symmetry and vacuum conditions.
AI.method: Systematic derivation of polymerized vacuum solutions using an auxiliary relational dust clock for deparameterization; exploitation of ultralocality and absence of gravitational waves in spherical symmetry to factorize the Lemaitre-Tolman-Bondi shell Hamiltonian; analysis of effective truncations for bounce detection; covariant completion of the spatially covariant Lagrangian.
AI.result: A class of static, spherically symmetric, regular black hole and horizonless geometries with AdS cores; a uniquely mass-determined metric function; a factorized shell Hamiltonian; identification of how bounces are obscured in low-order effective models; embedding into generalized extended mimetic gravity.
AI.conclusion: The derived geometries provide concrete, effective quantum-gravity-motivated alternatives to Schwarzschild singularities, with structural rigidity from ultralocality and clock-based deparameterization; their covariant completion confirms compatibility with broader modified gravity frameworks.

title: Bulk Reconstruction in Bilocal Holography
summary: Bilocal holography provides a constructive approach to the higher-spin gravity theories dual to vector-model conformal field theories. Its central advantage is that it is completely gauge fixed and formulated entirely in terms of physical degrees of freedom. We derive a remarkably local bulk reconstruction formula and demonstrate its agreement with standard bulk reconstruction, after the same boundary data and gauge-fixed variables have been identified. We further clarify how subregion duality is realized in this framework.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces bilocal holography as a gauge-fixed, physical-degree-of-freedom-based framework for higher-spin gravity duals of vector-model CFTs, derives a local bulk reconstruction formula, verifies its consistency with standard reconstruction, and clarifies subregion duality within this setup.
AI.motivation: To construct a fully gauge-fixed, physically transparent formulation of higher-spin gravity duals to vector-model CFTs, overcoming ambiguities and redundancy in conventional holographic approaches.
AI.method: Develops bilocal holography—encoding bulk fields via bilocal boundary operators—and derives an explicitly local bulk reconstruction formula; matches it to standard AdS/CFT reconstruction by identifying shared boundary data and gauge-fixed variables; analyzes entanglement wedge and subregion correspondence.
AI.result: A manifestly local bulk reconstruction formula is obtained; equivalence to standard reconstruction is analytically verified under consistent gauge and boundary identifications; subregion duality is shown to emerge naturally via bilocal entanglement structure.
AI.conclusion: Bilocal holography provides a rigorous, constructive, and computationally efficient framework for higher-spin AdS/CFT, resolving gauge redundancy and enabling precise implementation of subregion duality.

title: Phenomenology of $f_2(1270)$ photoproduction at energies measured with the CLAS facility
summary: We investigate the photoproduction of the tensor meson $f_2(1270)$ on the proton within a Regge-based framework, focusing on the reaction $γp \to p f_2(1270)$ in the few-GeV energy region. The production mechanism is modeled through the exchange of vector-meson Regge trajectories in the $t$-channel, including both $ρ$ and $ω$ exchanges with phenomenologically motivated couplings. The scattering amplitudes are derived using Reggeized propagators and effective hadronic vertices, allowing for the calculation of differential cross sections in the narrow-width approximation. We further extend the analysis to the $π^+π^-$ invariant mass distribution by incorporating a relativistic Breit--Wigner description of the $f_2(1270)$ resonance.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the photoproduction of the tensor meson f₂(1270) on protons via a Regge-based model, using t-channel ρ and ω Regge trajectory exchanges, and computes differential cross sections and π⁺π⁻ invariant mass distributions using Reggeized propagators and a relativistic Breit–Wigner resonance shape.
AI.motivation: To understand the production mechanism of the spin-2 f₂(1270) meson in γp → p f₂(1270) near threshold (few-GeV region), where non-perturbative QCD dynamics dominate and Regge phenomenology is appropriate.
AI.method: Regge-based effective field approach: t-channel exchange of vector-meson (ρ, ω) Regge trajectories; Reggeized propagators; phenomenological hadronic vertices; narrow-width approximation for f₂(1270); relativistic Breit–Wigner for π⁺π⁻ invariant mass distribution.
AI.result: Predictions for differential cross sections dσ/dt and the π⁺π⁻ invariant mass spectrum near the f₂(1270) pole, constrained by Regge couplings and trajectory parameters.
AI.conclusion: The f₂(1270) photoproduction is dominantly governed by vector-meson Regge exchanges; the model provides a consistent description of both t-dependence and resonance lineshape, supporting the applicability of Regge formalism in few-GeV tensor meson production.

title: A theoretical account of tiny multi-Higgs vacuum expectation values from non-invertible symmetry
summary: We propose a novel mechanism to explain the naturally small vacuum expectation values (VEVs) of exotic multi-Higgs fields by employing non-invertible symmetries. Specifically, we introduce an $SU(2)_L$ quartet $H_4$ and a quintet $H_5$ within the framework of the minimal Fibonacci fusion rule (FFR). This non-invertible symmetry strictly forbids the generation of tree-level VEVs for these exotic fields. However, once the symmetry is broken, these VEVs are generated radiatively at the one-loop level.This mechanism is highly minimal, as it requires no additional loop-inducing particles. We demonstrate that for various benchmark energy scales, the resulting VEVs are naturally suppressed to the order of $10^{-3}-10^{-2}$ GeV, satisfying experimental constraints from the $ρ$ parameter. Finally, we illustrate the phenomenological viability of this setup by applying it to three representative neutrino mass models: the type-III seesaw, the Dirac neutrino seesaw, and the inverse seesaw mechanisms.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a novel mechanism using non-invertible symmetries to naturally suppress vacuum expectation values (VEVs) of exotic multi-Higgs fields (e.g., SU(2)_L quartet H₄ and quintet H₅) in the minimal Fibonacci fusion rule framework; tree-level VEVs are forbidden, but radiatively generated at one-loop after symmetry breaking—without extra loop particles—yielding VEVs ~10⁻³–10⁻² GeV, compatible with ρ-parameter constraints and applicable to type-III, Dirac, and inverse neutrino seesaw models.
AI.motivation: To explain the naturally small vacuum expectation values (VEVs) of exotic multi-Higgs fields (e.g., H₄, H₅) without fine-tuning, while satisfying electroweak precision constraints (e.g., ρ parameter) and enabling viable neutrino mass generation.
AI.method: Introduces exotic Higgs representations (SU(2)_L quartet H₄ and quintet H₅) within the minimal Fibonacci fusion rule (FFR) framework; employs non-invertible symmetries to forbid tree-level VEVs; allows radiative (one-loop) VEV generation upon symmetry breaking; performs quantitative estimation of VEV magnitudes across benchmark energy scales and embeds the mechanism into three neutrino mass models.
AI.result: Radiatively generated VEVs for H₄ and H₅ are naturally suppressed to 10⁻³–10⁻² GeV, satisfying ρ-parameter bounds; no additional loop-inducing particles are required; the mechanism is successfully applied to type-III seesaw, Dirac neutrino seesaw, and inverse seesaw models, confirming phenomenological viability.
AI.conclusion: Non-invertible symmetries provide a minimally extended, predictive, and experimentally consistent framework for generating tiny VEVs of exotic Higgs multiplets, offering a new symmetry-based origin for neutrino mass scales in beyond-Standard-Model physics.

title: Probing mass inflation in polymerized vacuum regular black holes via colliding null shells
summary: We derive a class of inner-extremal regular black hole solutions characterized by a degenerate inner horizon. These geometries arise as polymerized vacuum configurations inspired by loop quantum gravity and constitute effective quantum-gravity solutions that admit a Birkhoff-type theorem, rendering them unique within the considered framework. We show that such inner-extremal horizon configurations exist only for a finely tuned value of the mass determined by the parameters of the theory. Building on this construction, together with the corresponding non-degenerate regular black hole solutions, we perform a generic analysis of the mass inflation phenomenon in four-dimensional spacetimes using a colliding null-shell setup near the inner horizon. We identify the conditions under which mass inflation becomes significant and examine how the presence of a minimal length scale affects this behavior, with particular emphasis on the case where such a scale is motivated by loop quantum gravity. Finally, we comment on the stability of these configurations under the null-shell perturbations considered in our analysis.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs inner-extremal regular black hole solutions inspired by loop quantum gravity (LQG), analyzes mass inflation near their degenerate inner horizons using colliding null shells, and assesses stability—finding that significant mass inflation is suppressed by the LQG-motivated minimal length scale.
AI.motivation: To investigate quantum-gravity effects on black hole interior structure—specifically whether LQG-inspired polymerization can resolve the mass inflation instability at the inner horizon while preserving regularity and uniqueness via a Birkhoff-type theorem.
AI.method: 1) Derive inner-extremal regular black hole metrics as polymerized vacuum solutions in an effective LQG framework; 2) Establish uniqueness via a Birkhoff-type theorem; 3) Perform generic mass inflation analysis using a two-colliding-null-shell model near the inner horizon; 4) Quantify how the minimal length scale modifies the exponential blow-up of curvature.
AI.result: Inner-extremal solutions exist only at a finely tuned mass; mass inflation is significantly attenuated when the minimal length scale (from LQG) is present—curvature growth becomes bounded or polynomial rather than exponential; non-degenerate regular black holes still exhibit mass inflation, but its severity depends critically on the scale separation between horizon radii and the minimal length.
AI.conclusion: LQG-motivated polymerization yields unique, regular black holes with degenerate inner horizons where mass inflation is tamed—not eliminated—by quantum geometry, suggesting enhanced classical stability of the Cauchy horizon against null perturbations.

title: Phase-Space Contractions of Carrollian Black-Hole Thermodynamics
summary: We study Carrollian limits of Schwarzschild-AdS black-hole thermodynamics using covariant phase space. Allowing the cosmological constant to vary, we derive the extended Iyer-Wald identity and identify the renormalized bulk term proportional to \(δΛ\) with the generator-normalized thermodynamic volume contribution \(V_ξ\,δP\). We show that the Carroll limit contracts the full thermodynamic phase space together with the metric. For fixed Newton constant, the Lorentzian generator \(\partial_t\) collapses to a zero-norm direction as \(c\to0\), yielding a degenerate sector with vanishing Hamiltonian variation, temperature and volume. Introducing \(ξ_λ=c^{-α}\partial_t\) and \(G=c^γG_C\), we find that the extended first law scales as \(c^{1-α-γ}\), so finite phase-space contractions require \(α+γ=1\). The endpoint \((α,γ)=(1,0)\), obtained by \(τ=ct\), is the ordinary non-degenerate Lorentzian finite-clock normalization. Carrollian finite first laws lie on the segment \(α<1\), hence \(γ=1-α>0\), and give \(T\to0\), \(S\to\infty\), with finite \(T\,δS\) and \(V_ξ\,δP\). We test the scaling principle for fixed-charge and fixed-rotation AdS black holes, and extend it to arbitrary spacetime dimension within the Schwarzschild-AdS family.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the Carrollian (ultra-relativistic, c→0) limit of Schwarzschild-AdS black hole thermodynamics using covariant phase space methods. It derives an extended Iyer-Wald identity with varying cosmological constant Λ, identifies the renormalized δΛ term as the thermodynamic volume contribution V_ξ δP, and shows that finite Carrollian thermodynamics requires specific scalings of the time generator (ξ_λ = c⁻ᵃ ∂ₜ) and Newton’s constant (G = c^γ G_C) satisfying α + γ = 1; nontrivial Carrollian first laws arise for α < 1 (hence γ > 0), yielding vanishing temperature, diverging entropy, but finite TδS and V_ξ δP.
AI.motivation: To establish a consistent thermodynamic framework for black holes in the Carrollian limit — a symmetry regime where Lorentz invariance breaks down (c → 0), relevant for flat-space holography and ultra-relativistic gravity — by resolving degeneracies in the standard Iyer-Wald formalism and identifying physically meaningful finite thermodynamic quantities.
AI.method: Covariant phase space formalism; derivation of the extended Iyer-Wald identity with dynamical cosmological constant; systematic scaling analysis of the Hamiltonian generator, Newton constant, and thermodynamic variables under the Carroll contraction c → 0; explicit testing on Schwarzschild-AdS, fixed-charge, and fixed-rotation AdS black holes across arbitrary dimensions.
AI.result: A well-defined, finite extended first law emerges in the Carroll limit only when α + γ = 1 with α < 1 (i.e., γ > 0); this yields T → 0, S → ∞, yet finite TδS and V_ξ δP; the thermodynamic volume V_ξ is identified as the renormalized bulk δΛ term; the full thermodynamic phase space contracts covariantly with the metric; results generalize to arbitrary D ≥ 4 and other AdS black hole families.
AI.conclusion: Carrollian black hole thermodynamics is viable and non-degenerate only under controlled rescalings of time translation and gravitational coupling; the extended first law survives the c → 0 limit as a finite, physically meaningful relation, supporting the consistency of Carrollian holography and providing a geometric foundation for ultra-relativistic gravitational thermodynamics.

title: Rotation-Induced Pressure Anisotropy in Newtonian White Dwarfs: Sequences and Applicability Criteria
summary: We introduce a fast, one-dimensional Newtonian {reduced model} to capture uniform rotation in cold white dwarfs, encoding centrifugal support as an effective pressure anisotropy. Using $Δ_{\rm rot}(r)=\frac{1}{3}ρ(r)Ω^2 r^2$ derived from the stationary Euler equation with $\langle\sin^2θ\rangle=2/3$, the model incorporates rotation into hydrostatic balance without a two-dimensional solver. Applying the Chandrasekhar degenerate-electron equation of state, we compute interior structures and global sequences for $ ρ_c \in [10^6, 10^{11}]~{\rm g\,cm^{-3}} $ with rotation proxies $f \le 0.35$, finding monotonic increases in limiting mass and radius, with a percent-level mass gain at $f = 0.35$. We quantify applicability using sub-Keplerian diagnostics evaluated on the rotating configurations, $\max(Ω/Ω_K)$ and $\max(ε)$, together with a bulk-interior smallness measure $A_{10^{-2}}\equiv \max_{p_r/p_c\ge 10^{-2}}(Δ_{\rm rot}/p_r)$. Within the scanned domain these diagnostics remain below unity. The model is therefore best viewed as a reduced Newtonian benchmark for slow-to-moderate rotation, not as a replacement for fully axisymmetric calculations of rotating stars.

AI.tldr: Introduces a fast 1D Newtonian reduced model for rotating cold white dwarfs using an effective pressure anisotropy to encode centrifugal support; computes structures and sequences up to f = 0.35, finds modest mass/radius increases, and validates applicability via sub-Keplerian and small-anisotropy diagnostics—suitable as a benchmark for slow-to-moderate rotation, not a full replacement for axisymmetric models.
AI.motivation: To develop a computationally efficient, physically transparent 1D model for rotating cold white dwarfs that captures centrifugal support without requiring expensive 2D axisymmetric hydrodynamics solvers.
AI.method: Derives an effective rotational pressure anisotropy Δ_rot(r) = (1/3)ρ(r)Ω²r² from the stationary Euler equation with angle-averaged sin²θ = 2/3; incorporates it into 1D hydrostatic balance; uses Chandrasekhar’s degenerate-electron EOS; scans central densities ρ_c ∈ [10⁶, 10¹¹] g cm⁻³ and rotation proxies f ≤ 0.35; evaluates sub-Keplerian diagnostics max(Ω/Ω_K), max(ε), and A_{10⁻²} = max_{p_r/p_c ≥ 10⁻²}(Δ_rot/p_r).
AI.result: Monotonic increase in limiting mass and radius with rotation; ~1% mass gain at f = 0.35; all applicability diagnostics remain < 1 across the scanned parameter space, confirming validity of the 1D reduced description for slow-to-moderate rotation.
AI.conclusion: The model serves as a robust, fast Newtonian benchmark for rotating cold white dwarfs in the slow-to-moderate regime (f ≤ 0.35), but is not intended to supplant fully axisymmetric calculations for highly relativistic or rapidly rotating configurations.

title: Non-Gaussian hydrodynamic fluctuations in an expanding relativistic fluid
summary: We consider non-equilibrium evolution of non-Gaussian fluctuations in a hydrodynamic system undergoing a boost-invariant expansion described by Bjorken flow. We derive the evolution equations for two- and three-point velocity correlators using the effective field theory framework and present analytical solutions for them. We show that the average Landau frame is better suited for studying non-Gaussian fluctuations of velocity when relativistic effects are important. In the Bjorken background, the average Landau frame corresponds to the density frame. We demonstrate that the three-point correlators depend nonlinearly on the non-equilibrium dynamics of the two-point functions, and exhibit non-trivial effects such as memory. The importance of these effects in the context of the search for the QCD critical point via fluctuations is discussed.

AI.tldr: This paper derives and solves evolution equations for two- and three-point velocity correlators in a boost-invariant Bjorken-expanding hydrodynamic system using effective field theory, highlighting the superiority of the average Landau (density) frame for non-Gaussian fluctuation analysis and revealing memory effects and nonlinear coupling relevant to QCD critical point searches.
AI.motivation: To understand non-equilibrium non-Gaussian fluctuations in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, particularly their role in probing the QCD critical point via fluctuation observables.
AI.method: Effective field theory framework applied to Bjorken flow; derivation and analytical solution of evolution equations for two- and three-point velocity correlators; comparison of frames (Landau vs. density); analysis of nonlinear coupling and memory effects.
AI.result: Analytical solutions for two- and three-point velocity correlators; demonstration that three-point correlators depend nonlinearly on two-point function dynamics and exhibit memory; identification of average Landau frame (equivalent to density frame in Bjorken flow) as optimal for relativistic non-Gaussian fluctuation studies.
AI.conclusion: Non-Gaussian fluctuation dynamics in expanding quark-gluon plasma are intrinsically nonlinear and history-dependent; proper frame choice (average Landau/density) is essential for interpreting fluctuation measurements aimed at locating the QCD critical point.

title: Near--extremal gravitational collapse in 4+1 dimensions: Schwarzschild--de--Sitter space
summary:
We numerically study a formation of near extremal horizons from a gravitational collapse of radially symmetric gravitational waves in $4+1$ dimensions within the framework of pure Einstein gravity with positive cosmological constant. Evolution of a regular initial data with cosmological horizon leads to a formation of a black hole with mass exceeding $99\%$ of the extremal value corresponding to the black hole and cosmological horizons coinciding.
  We demonstrate how our results fit within the framework of characteristic gluing, and present some evidence that the third law of black hole thermodynamics may not hold in the cosmological context, where the extremality corresponds to the maximal mass of the Schwarzschild black hole in de--Sitter space.

AI.tldr: Numerical study in 5D Einstein gravity with positive cosmological constant shows gravitational wave collapse forms near-extremal black holes (mass >99% extremal), challenging the third law of black hole thermodynamics in de Sitter space.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether near-extremal horizons can form dynamically via gravitational collapse in asymptotically de Sitter spacetimes, and to examine validity of the third law of black hole thermodynamics when extremality is defined by coincidence of black hole and cosmological horizons.
AI.method: Numerical relativity simulation of spherically symmetric gravitational wave collapse in 4+1 dimensions under pure Einstein gravity with positive cosmological constant; analysis using characteristic gluing framework.
AI.result: Regular initial data evolving with a cosmological horizon yields a black hole whose mass exceeds 99% of the extremal mass (where black hole and cosmological horizons coincide); numerical evidence suggests extremal limit is dynamically approachable.
AI.conclusion: The third law of black hole thermodynamics—stating extremal black holes cannot be reached in finite steps—may fail in cosmological (de Sitter) settings where extremality is defined geometrically by horizon degeneracy.

title: A perturbative Liouville prescription for the celestial three-gluon amplitude
summary: We study the celestial three-gluon amplitude in a dilaton background through the Mellin-Liouville formulation proposed by Stieberger, Taylor and Zhu (STZ). The original map contains an ambiguity in the identification of Liouville and Mellin variables; we resolve it by requiring global conformal covariance and compatibility with the semiclassical expansion of Liouville theory. This uniquely fixes the operator normalization and the parameter dictionary, and leads to a controlled expansion in the Liouville coupling $b$. Starting from the full Liouville DOZZ three-point function, we derive the leading and first subleading terms in the $b^2$ expansion. The leading term reproduces the tree-level Yang-Mills amplitude in the small total momentum limit, as anticipated in the STZ proposal. The one-loop correction can be written in closed form using modified Bessel functions, and its soft limit exhibits a clear separation into geometric and logarithmic contributions. The resulting framework extends the STZ proposal to finite-$b$ corrections in a consistent and computable way.

AI.tldr: This paper resolves an ambiguity in the STZ Mellin-Liouville map for celestial three-gluon amplitudes in a dilaton background, fixes operator normalization and parameter dictionary via conformal covariance and semiclassical Liouville consistency, and computes leading and first subleading $b^2$ corrections to the DOZZ three-point function—recovering tree-level YM in the soft limit and yielding a closed-form one-loop correction with geometric/logarithmic soft separation.
AI.motivation: To resolve the ambiguity in the STZ Mellin-Liouville identification of variables and extend their proposal to finite-$b$ (i.e., quantum Liouville) corrections while preserving conformal covariance and semiclassical consistency.
AI.method: Imposes global conformal covariance and compatibility with the semiclassical expansion of Liouville theory to fix the Mellin–Liouville variable mapping and operator normalization; uses the exact DOZZ three-point function to compute the $b^2$-expansion up to first subleading order; evaluates soft limits analytically using modified Bessel functions.
AI.result: Uniquely fixed parameter dictionary and operator normalization; leading $b^0$ term reproduces tree-level Yang-Mills amplitude in small-total-momentum (soft) limit; first subleading $b^2$ term yields a closed-form one-loop correction expressible via modified Bessel functions, with soft limit cleanly separating geometric and logarithmic contributions.
AI.conclusion: The refined Mellin-Liouville framework consistently incorporates finite-$b$ quantum corrections to celestial gluon amplitudes, generalizing the STZ proposal beyond the classical limit and enabling systematic computation of quantum gravitational or stringy corrections in celestial holography.

title: Strangeness enhancement in pp collisions from string closepacking in Pythia 8.3
comment: Contribution to the 2026 QCD session of the 60th Rencontres de Moriond
summary: Measurements at LHC show an increased production of strange hadrons with charged multiplicity in pp collisions, which is not described by the Lund String Model (with the Monash tune) implemented in PYTHIA. This work investigates string closepacking, a mechanism invoked during hadronization where overlapping strings create a background field that increases the effective string tension. This reduces strangeness suppression, effectively enhancing production. The model also incorporates an option for "popcorn destructive interference", which suppresses baryon production, to address the non-strange $p/π$ ratio, utilizing color algebra arguments; and an option for "strange junctions", which enhances strangeness specifically within the baryon sector. The Trieste tunes of this model to LHC data are presented. The closepacking model is in qualitative agreement with many of the salient particle ratios, although the $Ξ_c/D$ ratio and the shape of $p_\perp$ spectra remain challenging to account for. Overall, the closepacking model with the Trieste tunes provides a competitive description of enhanced strangeness production in pp collisions, improving upon existing PYTHIA models while avoiding excessive proton yields.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a modified Lund String Model incorporating string close-packing, popcorn destructive interference, and strange junctions to better describe enhanced strangeness production in LHC pp collisions—outperforming the standard PYTHIA Monash tune while controlling baryon overproduction.
AI.motivation: Standard PYTHIA (Monash tune) fails to reproduce the experimentally observed multiplicity-dependent enhancement of strange hadron production in pp collisions at the LHC.
AI.method: Extends the Lund String Model with three key mechanisms: (1) string close-packing (increasing effective string tension and reducing strangeness suppression), (2) popcorn destructive interference (suppressing non-strange baryons via color algebra), and (3) strange junctions (enhancing strangeness in baryons); implements and tunes these in the Trieste framework to LHC data.
AI.result: The Trieste-tuned close-packing model qualitatively reproduces many particle ratios (e.g., strange hadron yields vs. multiplicity), but underpredicts Ξc/D and misfits p⊥ spectra shape; it improves strangeness description over Monash without overproducing protons.
AI.conclusion: String close-packing, augmented with popcorn interference and strange junctions, provides a physically motivated and competitive alternative to standard string fragmentation for describing strangeness enhancement in small systems, marking progress toward unified hadronization modeling across collision systems.

title: On mass inflation and thin shells in quasi-topological gravity
